inventory:identity-trust.area: Identity and legal strength: recipient authentication (access code, SMS, phone, KBA, ID Verification incl. EU/UK and bank ID schemes), standards-based signatures (EU AES/QES, PAdES, trust lists), digital certificates, eSeal, Notary/RON, eWitness, 21 CFR Part 11, signature appearance, certificate of completion, envelope history, tamper evidence, retention and purge, data residency, encryption, Monitor

features.name: Access code authentication
features.what: The sender sets an alphanumeric code for a recipient and passes it on outside the email. The recipient must type it before any document opens.
features.ours_evidence: src/server/routes-sign.ts line 69 (document locked until a signed cookie for the code is present), lines 192-204 (check, cookie, audit 'Access code accepted'), line 179 frozenText with ACCESS_CODE_TRIES from src/lib/policy.ts (frozen after 10 wrong tries until the sender sets a new code). Certificate line 'Link sent by email and an access code chosen by the sender' in src/server/pdf.ts line 369. Gap: the code is stored as typed in recipients.access_code (src/server/db.ts line 64) and compared raw with safeEqual, not hashed.
features.docusign_tier: Not stated on the pages found in this run; described as a standard sender option.
features.honesty_risk: It only shows that whoever opened the document was told the code. Never call it identity verification. If we hash it later, do not claim it was always hashed.
features.provider_notes: None needed. Hashing the stored code (HMAC under APP_SECRET, as the one-time codes already are) is a small change.

features.name: SMS one-time passcode before opening
features.what: A one-time code is texted to a mobile number the sender typed; the recipient must enter it before the envelope opens. Recorded on the certificate and in the history.
features.ours_evidence: verify 'sms_code' in src/lib/checks.ts (CHECKS = none, email_code, sms_code; CHECK_PROVES wording), code issue/check/limits in src/server/signercode.ts, sending through Twilio with fetch or any provider via SMS_WEBHOOK_URL in src/server/sms.ts, masked number on the certificate (checkLine). Also a one-time code by email, which DocuSign does not list. Off until the operator configures a provider; README says Twilio and the hook were only tested against a stand-in (tests/signercode.test.ts).
features.docusign_tier: Phone Authentication (call or text) carries a per-use fee per DocuSign community answers; the developer page says recipient authentication may incur additional charges in production.
features.honesty_risk: Proves someone held that phone at that moment, and only as right as the number the sender typed. Not identity. Not an advanced signature.
features.provider_notes: Twilio or any SMS gateway behind SMS_WEBHOOK_URL. No free production option; the operator pays per text (SMS_DAILY_PER_ACCOUNT caps it). Remaining work is one real test in the provider's test mode.

features.name: Phone call one-time passcode (voice)
features.what: Instead of a text, an automated call reads the code out. In DocuSign's current Phone Authentication the recipient chooses call or text; DocuSign states 190 countries and over 70 languages. The legacy version let the sender pick SMS or call.
features.ours_evidence: src/server/sms.ts only sends texts (no call API); src/lib/checks.ts CHECKS has no call option; README 'What is not in it' lists 'checks by phone call' as not built.
features.docusign_tier: Per-use fee (community answers); part of Phone Authentication.
features.honesty_risk: Same as SMS: proves someone answered that line, not who they are. A spoken code can be overheard.
features.provider_notes: Twilio Programmable Voice works with the Twilio account the SMS code already uses (Calls API with TwiML Say); Vonage also. Asterisk or FreeSWITCH are open source but still need a paid SIP trunk. Useful for landlines, older people and people who cannot read texts; needs per-language speech and the same daily cost caps as texts.

features.name: Knowledge-based authentication (KBA)
features.what: The recipient answers questions drawn from public and commercial records (past addresses and the like) before opening. DocuSign uses LexisNexis Risk Solutions; neither DocuSign nor the sender can see or change the questions. US only.
features.ours_evidence: No code (grep for kba or knowledge-based in src finds only the 'not built' statements); README 'What is not in it' line 519; src/app/security/page.tsx line 161 'No check of identity documents'.
features.docusign_tier: Per-use fee; US customers only (developer page and support).
features.honesty_risk: Answers can be found or guessed from breached and public data; NIST SP 800-63B forbids knowledge-based questions as an authenticator. Never present KBA as strong identity proof.
features.provider_notes: LexisNexis Risk Solutions, Experian or Equifax, under a contract with a permissible-purpose review. No free or open option. US only, so little use to most of our users.

features.name: ID Verification: government photo ID check
features.what: The recipient photographs a passport, driving licence or ID card; a partner checks the document is genuine before the envelope opens. Admins choose which ID Verification configurations are offered. DocuSign lists eligible countries and IDs and says this standard method can back simple and advanced signatures.
features.ours_evidence: README 'What is not in it' line 519; src/lib/checks.ts CHECK_LIMITS 'None of these looks at a passport or an identity card'; no IDV code anywhere in src/server.
features.docusign_tier: Paid add-on to Standard or Business Pro, from US$2.50 per verification attempt (ISV pricing page as summarised by search); Standard includes a one-time bonus of 5 verifications (DocuSign plans blog).
features.honesty_risk: We would only repeat the provider's result; never say 'identity verified' beyond what the provider reports. ID images are personal data and a face is biometric (special category under GDPR Art. 9): a DPIA, retention limits and naming the provider on /security are needed.
features.provider_notes: Onfido (Entrust), Veriff, IDnow, Persona, Jumio or Stripe Identity, each paid per check with a contract. Open-source MRZ or OCR readers only read a document, they cannot tell a forgery, so there is no honest free option. The operator signs the provider contract and sets keys.

features.name: ID Verification with liveness (selfie video)
features.what: After the ID photo the recipient records a selfie video turning their head; the partner matches the face to the ID and checks a live person is present, with a trained agent reviewing doubtful cases. DocuSign says liveness configurations cannot produce QES.
features.ours_evidence: No face or selfie code in src (grep for selfie or liveness finds nothing).
features.docusign_tier: Part of the ID Verification add-on.
features.honesty_risk: Biometric data: explicit consent, a DPIA and a short retention period. Never claim we ourselves checked a face.
features.provider_notes: Same providers as the ID check (most sell document plus liveness as one flow). Size assumes the document check exists first.

features.name: ID Verification through bank IDs and national eIDs
features.what: The recipient proves who they are by logging in to their bank or a government eID scheme: itsme (Belgium), BankID (Norway, Sweden), MitID (Denmark), iDIN (Netherlands), Finnish Trust Network, OneID (UK).
features.ours_evidence: No eID scheme. src/server/oidc.ts already does an OpenID Connect code flow by hand (PKCE S256, RS256 ID token checked against published keys, issuer, audience, nonce) for Google and Microsoft sender sign-in, which most eID brokers also speak.
features.docusign_tier: Part of ID Verification (add-on).
features.honesty_risk: Say which scheme vouched and what it returned (name, maybe date of birth), nothing more. Never imply a qualified signature unless a QTSP issues one.
features.provider_notes: Brokers such as Signicat, Criipto or Scrive eID Hub (paid per login, test tiers exist), or direct scheme contracts. A public body may already have its national login (for example GOV.UK One Login for UK central government services) under its own agreement. The EU Digital Identity Wallet (member states must offer one) is an emerging option to watch. Reusing src/server/oidc.ts keeps the code small; very high value in the Nordics and Benelux.

features.name: ID Verification with NFC chip reading
features.what: The recipient scans the chip in their ID with a phone: German eID through IDnow, IC-chip reading for Japan and Australia/New Zealand.
features.ours_evidence: Nothing in src; the product is browser only (README 'native mobile apps' not built).
features.docusign_tier: Part of ID Verification (add-on); country specific.
features.honesty_risk: Do not claim chip verification from a web page: browsers cannot read passport or ID chips (Web NFC reads NDEF tags only).
features.provider_notes: A provider SDK in a native app (IDnow, Onfido and others offer NFC SDKs), or the provider's own app handing back a result. German eID through AusweisApp needs an eID service provider authorisation.

features.name: Identity Wallet (reusable verified identity)
features.what: A person stores a verified identity once and reuses it across agreements, shortening later signings; DocuSign has a separate privacy notice for its Identity Wallet for QES.
features.ours_evidence: Nothing in src. Saved signature pictures for account holders exist, which is not an identity.
features.docusign_tier: Part of the Identify / ID Verification offering; plan not stated.
features.honesty_risk: Holding verified identity data makes us a far bigger target and a controller of sensitive data. Never store it without a legal basis and a deletion rule.
features.provider_notes: Better to accept the EU Digital Identity Wallet or a provider's reusable identity than to build our own wallet.

features.name: UK Right to Work digital identity check
features.what: A ready-made workflow for UK employers that checks UK and Irish passports through Onfido, a certified digital verification service under the UK trust framework, and captures Home Office share codes for others. Needs the ID Verification add-on.
features.ours_evidence: Nothing in src.
features.docusign_tier: Maestro template plus the ID Verification add-on.
features.honesty_risk: Only a certified identity service provider's check counts for right to work. Never call our own flow certified or say it gives the employer a statutory excuse.
features.provider_notes: Contract with an IDSP on the UK government register (Onfido, Yoti, TrustID and others). Useful for UK charities hiring staff and volunteers.

features.name: ID Verification for EU Qualified Signatures
features.what: Identity proofing equivalent to face to face, done by a certified agent or video identification (IDnow VideoIdent or eID), as eIDAS requires before a qualified certificate is issued.
features.ours_evidence: Nothing in src; src/app/help/outside.tsx line 47 says Sign&Grow does not make qualified signatures.
features.docusign_tier: Part of the QES offering (contact sales).
features.honesty_risk: Only a QTSP's own proofing counts. Never run our own video call and call it qualified identification.
features.provider_notes: Comes bundled with a QTSP's remote QES service (IDnow, Namirial, InfoCert, Swisscom Trust Services and others). Not something to build apart from QES.

features.name: EU Advanced Electronic Signature (AES)
features.what: A per-signer certificate and a cryptographic PAdES signature in the PDF so the signature is uniquely linked to the signer and any later change is detectable. DocuSign's AES provider uses OpenTrust (DocuSign France) certificates, with a one-time code or SMS as part of the flow; DocuSign mixes simple, AES and QES signers in one envelope.
features.ours_evidence: No PKI code: grep for PAdES, PKCS7, signpdf, X.509, ByteRange in src finds only help text. package.json has pdf-lib but no signing library. README 'What is not in it' line 512 'Certificate-based digital signatures... not advanced or qualified signatures under eIDAS'. src/app/security/page.tsx line 159 says so publicly.
features.docusign_tier: Standards-based signatures; plan not stated in the pages found (sold through sales).
features.honesty_risk: Whether a signature is 'advanced' under eIDAS Art. 26 is a legal judgement about identification and sole control, not a file format. Never label output AES without a QTSP or lawyer standing behind it.
features.provider_notes: Practical route is a QTSP's AES or remote signing service through the open Cloud Signature Consortium API (Swisscom, Namirial, InfoCert, D-Trust and others; paid). The PAdES part is buildable with open code (pdf-lib plus @signpdf or PKI.js, and the EU's open-source DSS library for validation).

features.name: EU Qualified Electronic Signature (QES)
features.what: A signature made with a qualified certificate from a Qualified Trust Service Provider on a qualified signature creation device; in EU law it has the effect of a handwritten signature (eIDAS Art. 25.2). DocuSign offers IDnow EU Qualified, DocuSign ID Verification for EU Qualified, and Signer Held EU Qualified.
features.ours_evidence: src/app/help/outside.tsx line 47 and src/lib/paperwork.ts lines 57, 199-204 say Sign&Grow does not provide qualified signatures; the check before sending (src/server/warnings.ts, src/lib/paperwork.ts) warns when a document likely needs one.
features.docusign_tier: Standards-based signatures, through sales; per-signature QTSP fees.
features.honesty_risk: Only the QTSP makes a QES. We would be the workflow around it. Never say 'our qualified signature' or show a QES badge unless the QTSP's signature validates against the EU Trusted List.
features.provider_notes: Contract with a QTSP offering remote QES over the CSC API (Namirial, InfoCert, Swisscom, D-Trust, Evrotrust, Certum; paid per signature, usually with their own identification). High value for EU public bodies, where written form often means QES.

features.name: Signer-held certificates (smart cards, national eID cards, US PIV)
features.what: The signer signs with a certificate they already hold: DocuSign lists 'Signer Held EU Qualified' and a US PIV card provider among standards-based signature types.
features.ours_evidence: No certificate handling in src; signing is a picture on the page (src/components/SignaturePad.tsx, src/server/pdf.ts drawField).
features.docusign_tier: Standards-based signatures (sales).
features.honesty_risk: We only carry the signature the card made; its legal level depends on the certificate. Validate it before showing any level.
features.provider_notes: Browsers cannot reach a smart card alone. Web eID (open source, MIT, from Estonia's RIA) needs its native app and browser extension on the signer's computer and supports several EU national ID cards, whose QES is free to citizens (for example Estonia, Belgium, Portugal). US federal PIV/CAC needs middleware too. Very useful for public bodies whose staff already carry such cards.

features.name: Country-specific certificate signatures (ICP-Brasil, India eSign/eMudhra, Mexico NOM 151)
features.what: Signature or seal types tied to a national PKI or rule: ICP-Brasil certificates, eMudhra Class-3 signatures and eSeals in India, NOM 151 compliant seals in Mexico.
features.ours_evidence: src/lib/paperwork.ts line 246 tells Brazilian users that ICP-Brasil qualified signatures are not provided; no code.
features.docusign_tier: Standards-based signatures (sales).
features.honesty_risk: Never claim a national legal level without the licensed provider's signature in the file.
features.provider_notes: One contract per country with a licensed CA or provider (ICP-Brasil CAs, eMudhra or other Indian eSign ASPs, a Mexican NOM 151 PSC). Do one country only when a real customer asks.

features.name: Platform-issued certificate per signature (ds_email)
features.what: DocuSign's 'ds_email' provider is a DocuSign-generated signature with a certificate, so each signature carries PKI evidence even at the simple level.
features.ours_evidence: No certificates; integrity rests on the SHA-256 of the signed file, the hash-chained audit trail (verifyChain in src/server/envelopes.ts line 62) and /verify (src/server/routes-account.ts line 706).
features.docusign_tier: Standards-based signatures (sales).
features.honesty_risk: A certificate from our own CA does not make a signature advanced or qualified and is not trusted by Acrobat by default. Say what it proves: that our server applied it at that time.
features.provider_notes: Own CA with node:crypto plus PKI.js or node-forge, key in an HSM or cloud KMS. Adds little over a single document seal for our users.

features.name: PAdES signature format with long-term validation
features.what: Signatures inside the PDF to ETSI EN 319 142 (PAdES), B-B for the base level and B-LT for qualified signatures, with validation data embedded so the signature can be checked years later.
features.ours_evidence: renderEnvelopePdf in src/server/pdf.ts lines 578-626 ends with pdf-lib doc.save(): no signature dictionary, no ByteRange, no DSS.
features.docusign_tier: Standards-based signatures (sales).
features.honesty_risk: The format alone is not a legal level. Do not say PAdES-compliant without testing against the EU DSS validator.
features.provider_notes: Open: pdf-lib plus @signpdf (MIT) or a CMS built with PKI.js; OCSP and CRL fetched from the issuing CA; validate with the EU DSS demo or library (LGPL). Needed by every seal or certificate entry here.

features.name: Trusted timestamps (RFC 3161, qualified time stamps)
features.what: An independent time-stamp authority signs the moment a document or signature existed. DocuSign France is listed as providing qualified time stamps.
features.ours_evidence: Times come from the server clock only (now() in src/server/util.ts, printed as UTC on the certificate in src/server/pdf.ts); no TSA call anywhere.
features.docusign_tier: Part of standards-based signatures and trust services; plan not stated.
features.honesty_risk: A free TSA timestamp is evidence of time, not a 'qualified' time stamp. Only call it qualified if the TSA is a QTSP on the EU Trusted List.
features.provider_notes: Free RFC 3161 services exist (FreeTSA.org; public timestamp servers run by DigiCert and Sectigo for code signing, check their terms). Qualified time stamps need a paid QTSP. Can also timestamp the audit chain head, which answers the CHAIN_TRUTH weakness that the operator could rewrite the chain.

features.name: Accepting certificates from any TSP on the EU Trusted List
features.what: DocuSign accepts qualified certificates issued by any Trust Service Provider on the EU Trust List and publishes lists of accepted providers by region.
features.ours_evidence: No certificate validation in src.
features.docusign_tier: Standards-based signatures (sales).
features.honesty_risk: Show the validator's result as it is, including 'indeterminate'. Never turn a partial check into a green tick.
features.provider_notes: The EU List of Trusted Lists is public and free; the EU DSS library (open source, Java) validates against it. Only worth it together with signer-held or QTSP signatures.

features.name: Being a Qualified Trust Service Provider on the EU Trusted List
features.what: DocuSign France SAS is on the French trusted list (ANSSI) as a QTSP, issuing QES, qualified time stamps, AES and advanced seals recognised in every member state.
features.ours_evidence: Not applicable to the code; README and /security say no certification.
features.docusign_tier: Company-level status, not a plan feature.
features.honesty_risk: Never suggest we are, or are close to being, a trust service provider.
features.provider_notes: Needs conformity assessment by an accredited body, supervision, insurance, HSMs and audits at least every 24 months. Not sensible for this team: partner with a QTSP instead.

features.name: Tamper-evident PKI seal on completed documents
features.what: Completed documents are digitally sealed with PKI so Acrobat shows the file is unchanged since signing; the certificate of completion says when it was signed.
features.ours_evidence: Integrity without PKI: SHA-256 of the signed PDF in every completion email, public /verify byte-for-byte check (POST /public/verify in src/server/routes-account.ts line 706) and /verify?id lookup (src/server/routes-evidence.ts line 65), hash-chained audit with chain head on the certificate (src/server/pdf.ts lines 403-412, CHAIN_TRUTH and MATCH_MEANS in src/lib/evidence.ts). No PDF digital signature: pdf.ts saves with pdf-lib only; README line 512.
features.docusign_tier: Standard on completed envelopes (described as part of the product, no plan named).
features.honesty_risk: A seal shows the file is unchanged since we sealed it, not who was behind each signature. Never promise the Acrobat green tick unless the certificate chains to the Adobe Approved Trust List; never call it a qualified seal.
features.provider_notes: Can be built alone with a certificate we control (Acrobat then shows 'validity unknown'). For a trusted tick, buy an AATL document signing certificate (GlobalSign, Entrust, DigiCert and others; paid yearly) whose key must sit in an HSM such as a cloud KMS. Add an RFC 3161 timestamp. Public bodies routinely look at Acrobat's signature panel, so this is one of the highest-value gaps.

features.name: eSeal: electronic seals for organisations
features.what: A seal is a recipient that is a legal entity, not a person: it is applied automatically in the order set, with no one clicking. Types: basic seal, legal person seal, EU advanced electronic seal (with onboarding; its CA is on the AATL). Seals are bound to the account that owns them.
features.ours_evidence: No seal recipient. A picture 'stamp' is being built right now (src/lib/stamps.ts, src/lib/stampink.ts, tables stamp_images and stamps in src/server/db.ts line 427) and its own words say it 'is not a certified electronic seal' (STAMP_IS).
features.docusign_tier: Standards-based signatures and seals (sales).
features.honesty_risk: Keep a picture stamp and a cryptographic seal clearly apart. A seal with our own or the organisation's ordinary certificate is a 'basic' seal: never call it advanced or qualified.
features.provider_notes: A basic organisation seal (PAdES with a certificate the organisation uploads as PKCS#12 or keeps in a KMS) is buildable alone. An EU advanced or qualified seal needs a certificate from a QTSP (paid, with organisation vetting). High value for public bodies issuing permits, certificates and letters at volume.

features.name: Stamps (company stamp or hanko)
features.what: An admin setting lets the account's users adopt a stamp (as used in Japan and elsewhere) in place of or next to a signature.
features.ours_evidence: In progress by another engineer: src/lib/stamps.ts (limits, 10 stamps per account, sizes, honest wording), src/lib/stampink.ts (paper removal, ink, texture), src/server/stamp.ts, tables stamp_images and stamps; the field through the envelope flow, screens and tests are still listed as pending.
features.docusign_tier: Account setting; plan not stated.
features.honesty_risk: As STAMP_IS says: a picture someone put on the document, not checked and not an electronic seal.
features.provider_notes: None.

features.name: Remote online notarization (DocuSign Notary)
features.what: A commissioned notary notarises over audio and video; an audio-visual recording is kept 10 years; DocuSign issues digital certificates for notaries; customers bring their own notaries; only in supported US states, and some states need the RON tool registered.
features.ours_evidence: README 'What is not in it' line 522; the check before sending (src/lib/paperwork.ts, src/server/warnings.ts) warns that some documents need a notary.
features.docusign_tier: Separate Notary product; DocuSign says it fits organisations notarising 200 or more documents a year; sales.
features.honesty_risk: Never call anything here notarised. State rules (identity proofing, recording, journal, retention) decide validity.
features.provider_notes: Needs commissioned notaries, state RON registration, video recording and storage, credential analysis and KBA. US only. Better to link out to a RON provider.

features.name: Notary On-Demand (notaries supplied by a partner)
features.what: Notarisation by partner notaries (OneNotary) without having your own, from US$25 per notarisation.
features.ours_evidence: Nothing in src.
features.docusign_tier: Pay per notarisation, from US$25.
features.honesty_risk: We would hand off to the notary service; the notarisation is theirs, not ours.
features.provider_notes: OneNotary, Proof (Notarize) and similar offer APIs; paid per session; US only.

features.name: eWitness (witnessed signing)
features.what: A witness recipient for a signer: the sender names the witness or leaves it for the signer to name (name, email, phone when two-factor is required). Up to two witnesses per signer. Needs a plan with eWitness and an admin switch. DocuSign does not enforce that signer and witness are together.
features.ours_evidence: Role 'witness' with witness_for and named_by_signer (src/server/witness.ts, src/lib/witness.ts, tests/witness.test.ts): asked right after the signer signs, a presence statement or 'I was not there', certificate lines (witnessCertLines in src/server/pdf.ts line 354), same-device flag, one-time code by email for the witness (src/lib/witness.ts line 102). Gap: one witness per signer only (src/lib/witness.ts line 100 'A person who signs has one witness on Sign&Grow').
features.docusign_tier: Plans that include eWitness (community says Business Pro and up), admin must enable it.
features.honesty_risk: We record what the witness states and cannot check presence. Never say an e-witnessed signature meets a law's witnessing rule; wills in many places need two witnesses physically present and usually ink.
features.provider_notes: None. Allowing two witnesses touches every rule that assumes one (witnessOf, ordering, certificate, set-aside on change).

features.name: 21 CFR Part 11: signing reason at each signature
features.what: In a Part 11 account each signature or initial requires the signer to pick a reason for signing (for example approval, review, authorship).
features.ours_evidence: No reason field: grep for 'signing reason', 'part 11', '21 cfr' in src finds nothing; field types in src/server/pdf.ts drawField have none.
features.docusign_tier: Life Sciences (Part 11) module, an add-on.
features.honesty_risk: A reason field alone is not Part 11 compliance.
features.provider_notes: None.

features.name: 21 CFR Part 11: re-authentication at signing
features.what: Signers authenticate again at each signature (or, with Rapid Part 11 signing, once to access and once to complete), separate from the login to view; Part 11 signers sign in with an account.
features.ours_evidence: Signers need no account (README 'No account and no app needed'); a passed one-time code opens the document for 24 hours (README 'Checking who signs'); nothing asks again at Finish.
features.docusign_tier: Life Sciences (Part 11) module.
features.honesty_risk: Do not claim the two-component rule of 11.200 is met unless the signer has a unique account with a password or equivalent.
features.provider_notes: Could reuse sender login, two-step codes (src/server/twostep.ts) or a fresh one-time code at Finish.

features.name: 21 CFR Part 11: signature manifestation
features.what: Under each signature image: the printed name of the signer, date and time of signing, the reason, and a unique identifier, on screen and on paper.
features.ours_evidence: Under a signature only 'Signed via Sign&Grow' and 8 characters of the recipient id (src/server/pdf.ts line 197); name and times are on the certificate, not under the signature.
features.docusign_tier: Life Sciences (Part 11) module.
features.honesty_risk: Same as the other Part 11 items.
features.provider_notes: None.

features.name: 21 CFR Part 11 account and validation documentation (Life Sciences module)
features.what: A Part 11 configured account with the controls above plus documentation that helps regulated customers validate the system.
features.ours_evidence: Nothing in src or README.
features.docusign_tier: Life Sciences module add-on.
features.honesty_risk: Never say 'Part 11 compliant': compliance belongs to the regulated user's validated system and procedures. Say 'features that support Part 11'.
features.provider_notes: Validation packs (IQ/OQ/PQ scripts, traceability) are documents we can write; an outside quality consultant review is advisable.

features.name: Envelope ID on the document pages
features.what: Account setting to print the Envelope ID on documents, with a default for every envelope; per-envelope override in the API (envelopeIdStamping).
features.ours_evidence: Every page gets 'Sign&Grow Envelope ID: env_...' (src/server/pdf.ts line 608), and /verify?id looks it up (src/server/routes-evidence.ts line 65). Always on, no setting.
features.docusign_tier: Account setting; plan not stated.
features.honesty_risk: The ID is not a secret and shows nothing about who signed.
features.provider_notes: None.

features.name: Signature adoption configuration
features.what: Admins can switch off typed styles and signature upload account-wide, so signers must draw (Settings, Signing Settings, Signature Adoption Configuration); on some paid plans only.
features.ours_evidence: Signers always may type, draw or upload (README 'Signing'; src/components/SignaturePad.tsx); grep for an admin restriction finds nothing. The certificate does not say how a signature was adopted (src/server/pdf.ts drawCertificate).
features.docusign_tier: Account setting on some paid plans (community answers only; no primary page found).
features.honesty_risk: A drawn signature is not a handwritten one and proves no identity. Do not imply drawing is safer.
features.provider_notes: None. Recording 'typed, drawn or uploaded' on the certificate is a small addition.

features.name: Certificate of completion
features.what: An electronic record drawn from the audit trail: who signed, when and where, authentication used, events (sent, viewed, signed, declined); downloadable, and an account setting attaches it to the completion email or combined PDF.
features.ours_evidence: drawCertificate in src/server/pdf.ts lines 314-436: envelope, documents with SHA-256 of originals, each recipient with role, times (UTC and local zone), identity check line, consent time, IP, signature image, witness lines, group, full audit trail and chain head; always appended to the signed PDF that everyone is emailed. /security/certificate explains every line (CERTIFICATE_PAGE_VERSION in src/lib/evidence.ts). Evidence pack ZIP (GET /envelopes/:id/evidence, src/server/routes-evidence.ts line 45).
features.docusign_tier: All plans.
features.honesty_risk: Names are those the sender typed; an IP is a connection, not a place (WHO_WHEN_WHERE in src/lib/evidence.ts). Keep saying so.
features.provider_notes: None.

features.name: Envelope history and audit events API
features.what: Actions, History shows every event of an envelope and can be printed; the API listAuditEvents returns them per envelope.
features.ours_evidence: Envelope page 'Audit trail' section with 'Record intact' or 'Record was altered' badge (src/app/app/envelopes/[id]/page.tsx lines 303-310); GET /envelopes/:id returns audit and chain (src/server/routes-envelopes.ts line 291); evidence pack has it as text and JSON with chain values.
features.docusign_tier: All plans.
features.honesty_risk: The chain has no secret key; whoever can write the database could rewrite it (CHAIN_TRUTH). Keep that sentence.
features.provider_notes: None.

features.name: Authoritative Copy
features.what: An account option for keeping one authoritative copy of a document (for transferable records); when on, documents are not attached to completion emails.
features.ours_evidence: Nothing in src; every signer gets the completed copy by email.
features.docusign_tier: Not stated; only mentioned in passing on the support page found.
features.honesty_risk: Never claim a document is a transferable record or an authoritative copy.
features.provider_notes: Needs an eVault design that meets UETA section 16 and ESIGN section 201 and usually a specialist custodian. Not for our users.

features.name: Document retention policy (automatic purge)
features.what: Admins set 'Keep for this many days' (up to 9,999) counted from completion, void or decline; envelopes then go to a purge queue (about 14 days) with notifications; options to also remove fields and metadata and redact personal data; switching the policy off pulls queued envelopes back.
features.ours_evidence: No retention setting: grep for retention or purge finds only account closing (purgeClosedAccounts and purgeUser in src/server/routes-trust.ts) and fixed clocks (MAIL_COPY_DAYS 90, SUPPORT_KEEP_DAYS 90 in src/lib/policy.ts; FINGERPRINT_KEPT_DAYS 365 in src/lib/evidence.ts). Envelopes stay until the sender deletes them.
features.docusign_tier: Admin setting; plan not stated in the pages found.
features.honesty_risk: Say what is not purged: backups until their own schedule, copies already emailed to recipients, the fingerprint kept a year for /verify. Never say 'deleted everywhere'.
features.provider_notes: None. Public bodies have retention schedules and GDPR storage limitation, so this matters.

features.name: Targeted purge with redaction
features.what: The sender (or someone acting for them, with purge permission) purges a completed, declined or voided envelope: documents only, documents and metadata, or also redact personal data (names, emails, IPs become 'Redacted' in the certificate and history). Irreversible redaction; 14-day queue.
features.ours_evidence: DELETE /envelopes/:id (src/server/routes-envelopes.ts lines 341-360) deletes it, or only hides it from the sender when recipients keep a copy (keptOnDelete), with POST /envelopes/:id/restore (line 373). No level choice, no redaction of personal data while keeping the record, no queue.
features.docusign_tier: Admin and sender permission; plan not stated.
features.honesty_risk: A redacted record proves much less; say so on the envelope and in /verify answers.
features.provider_notes: None.

features.name: Data residency (choice of region)
features.what: eSignature accounts can live in US, Canada, Europe, Australia or Japan data centres; region set at sign-up by billing address or chosen with a representative; several accounts can be in different regions; agreement data stays at rest in region while some metadata such as names and audit metadata can leave.
features.ours_evidence: One region per server, stated by the operator in DATA_REGION, DATA_HOST, DATA_BACKUPS and printed on /security and /security/processing (src/lib/dataplace.ts lines 57-70, src/app/security/DataPlace.tsx); README says 'one region for everything, because storage is one disk'. No per-account region and no routing between servers.
features.docusign_tier: All plans (region by sign-up location).
features.honesty_risk: Name every processor outside the region (mail, SMS, payment, any AI chat model). Never say 'your data never leaves X' while email or texts go through a provider elsewhere.
features.provider_notes: Software side is ours: one deployment per region plus a directory that sends each account to its home server. The operator rents hosting in each region (for example an EU host such as Hetzner or OVH, OVH or a large cloud in Canada, a large cloud in Australia and Japan) and ideally a mail and SMS provider per region. Public bodies in Canada, Australia and the EU often require in-country storage.

features.name: Encryption at rest for documents
features.what: Documents are encrypted with AES-256 (or equivalent) on upload as a default, under managed keys; contract security attachment commits to it.
features.ours_evidence: AES-256-GCM per-file keys (HKDF) for every stored file when FILE_ENCRYPTION_KEY is set, with rotation and a safe migration script (src/server/filecrypt.ts line 75, src/server/filestore.ts, scripts/encrypt-files.mjs). Off by default; the SQLite database (names, field values, signature pictures, audit) is not encrypted by the app (README 'Encrypting stored files'); another engineer is currently adding encryption of extracted document text.
features.docusign_tier: All plans.
features.honesty_risk: The key sits in the server's settings, so this protects a stolen disk or leaked backup, not a break-in to the running server. Never say 'end-to-end' or 'we cannot read your documents'.
features.provider_notes: SQLCipher (open source) or field-level encryption for the database; making file encryption the default for new installs.

features.name: Customer-controlled encryption keys
features.what: Customers who adopt the Security Appliance (hybrid cloud appliance) can control the encryption keys on their documents.
features.ours_evidence: One server key for all accounts (FILE_ENCRYPTION_KEY, src/server/filestore.ts); no per-account key.
features.docusign_tier: Security Appliance (hybrid cloud appliance) add-on.
features.honesty_risk: The server still decrypts to render and stamp; say the customer can revoke access by revoking the key, not that we never see content.
features.provider_notes: Per-account keys wrapped by the customer's KMS (AWS KMS, Google Cloud KMS, Azure Key Vault) or by HashiCorp Vault or OpenBao (open source) that the customer runs. Mostly for large public bodies.

features.name: Monitor: account activity tracking and alerts
features.what: 24/7 tracking of web, mobile and API account activity (login attempts, password changes, envelope deletions and more) with pre-built alerts for suspicious activity, compromised-credential tracking, data kept ten years.
features.ours_evidence: Per person only: list of signed-in browsers (src/app/app/settings/SignedIn.tsx), a log of two-step changes (two_step_log in src/server/db.ts line 385, shown by src/server/routes-twostep.ts line 141), email to the owner when a new way in is connected (README 'Signing in with Google or Microsoft'), emails to teams about API keys (tellTeamsAboutKeys in src/server/routes-trust.ts), operator alerts in the operator queue. No account-wide security event log for admins and no alert rules.
features.docusign_tier: Monitor is a separate add-on (enterprise).
features.honesty_risk: Do not call it 24/7 monitoring unless a person watches it. Say which events are logged.
features.provider_notes: None for the log and alerts.

features.name: Monitor API for SIEM export
features.what: Pull API (getStream, up to 2,000 records per call, not filterable) for an organisation admin, to feed a SIEM; custom alerts are built in the SIEM; no webhooks.
features.ours_evidence: No security event stream; existing webhooks (src/server/webhooks.ts) carry envelope events only; grep for SIEM or syslog finds nothing.
features.docusign_tier: Monitor add-on.
features.honesty_risk: None beyond accuracy of what is exported.
features.provider_notes: Once the event log exists: a paged JSON endpoint for admin-scope keys plus the existing signed webhooks; optional syslog or OpenTelemetry output. Government security teams ask for this.

features.name: Compromised credential checks
features.what: Monitor tracks compromised credentials found on the dark web for the account's users.
features.ours_evidence: No breached-password check at sign-up or password change (grep for pwned or breach finds none in src/server).
features.docusign_tier: Monitor add-on.
features.honesty_risk: A clean result does not mean a password is safe. Never call it dark web monitoring unless a service actually monitors.
features.provider_notes: Have I Been Pwned's Pwned Passwords range API is free and sends only the first 5 characters of a SHA-1 hash (k-anonymity). Address breach monitoring needs a paid HIBP key.

features.name: Security certifications and government authorisations
features.what: ISO 27001 certified security programme; Docusign Federal (eSignature) holds FedRAMP Moderate, DoD Impact Level 4 provisional authorisation and GovRAMP; GSA OneGov offers 70 percent off FedRAMP and IL4 plans until 31 January 2027.
features.ours_evidence: README 'What is not in it': 'A security certification' not built; /security lists only what the code does.
features.docusign_tier: Docusign Federal and Enterprise Pro FedRAMP or IL4 plans for government.
features.honesty_risk: Never claim ISO 27001, SOC 2, FedRAMP, GovRAMP, IL4, G-Cloud, IRAP or similar until the audit or authorisation is granted; 'aligned with' is also misleading.
features.provider_notes: Needs an audit firm or accredited assessor (3PAO for FedRAMP), a sponsoring agency, continuous monitoring and hosting that is itself authorised. For many public bodies this is the procurement gate, more than any feature. A self-hosted deployment run by the public body on its own authorised infrastructure is a cheaper path to raise later.

features.name: SMS delivery of the signing link
features.what: The envelope notification goes by text instead of or as well as email; recipients must have consented; at most about 10 SMS or WhatsApp recipients per envelope; SMS delivery cannot be combined with SMS or phone authentication for the same person.
features.ours_evidence: 'Also text the signing link' (text_link) with reminders by text at most daily and 4 texts a day per number (README 'Checking who signs'; src/server/signercode.ts, src/server/envelopes.ts, src/server/bysender.ts).
features.docusign_tier: Multi-channel delivery add-on to Standard and up, from US$0.40 per delivery (ISV pricing page as summarised); Standard gets 5 one-time bonus deliveries.
features.honesty_risk: 'Sent' means the provider took the text, not that it arrived (README already says this).
features.provider_notes: Same SMS provider as the one-time code.

features.name: WhatsApp delivery of the signing link
features.what: The notification goes by WhatsApp (or email plus WhatsApp); not together with SMS for one recipient; not for signing groups.
features.ours_evidence: No WhatsApp sending by the server. The sender can share a recipient's link through WhatsApp themselves ('Share on WhatsApp' in src/components/sender/OwnLink.tsx line 46, 'I will send the link myself' in src/lib/bysender.ts).
features.docusign_tier: Multi-channel delivery add-on.
features.honesty_risk: Business-initiated WhatsApp messages need pre-approved templates and the person's opt-in; never message without consent.
features.provider_notes: Meta WhatsApp Business Platform directly or through Twilio, Vonage or 360dialog; business verification and per-conversation fees. Very useful for charities working where WhatsApp replaces email.

inventory:identity-trust.notes:
How the research was done: WebFetch could not reach DocuSign (developers.docusign.com and ecom.docusign.com do not resolve in this cloud session; they, support.docusign.com and docusign.com would have to be allowed in the session's network settings to read the pages directly). Every DocuSign fact above comes from web search summaries of the DocuSign URLs listed in sources, not from my own reading of those pages, so check exact wording, plan names and prices on the live pages before quoting them. The shared web search budget ran out before I could check two things, which I left out as features: (1) whether admins can customise the Electronic Record and Signature Disclosure, (2) whether the certificate of completion prints how each signature was adopted (typed, drawn, uploaded). Both are commonly seen in DocuSign but unsourced here. Left out on purpose: DocuSign Signature Appliance (on-premises PKI hardware, retired July 2023: https://www.docusign.com/blog/developers/docusign-signature-appliance-to-be-retired-july-2023) and mobile driver's licence support (announced as coming soon, not shipped).

Code checks (read only, nothing changed; scratch dir /tmp/gap-identity created and empty): README claims in this area match the code. Access codes, email and SMS one-time codes, witnesses, certificate of completion, hash-chained audit, /verify, evidence pack, file encryption and the data-place settings are all there as described. One detail the README does not mention: access codes are stored and compared as typed (src/server/db.ts line 64, src/server/routes-sign.ts line 197). Work in progress by other engineers touches this area: picture stamps (src/lib/stamps.ts, src/lib/stampink.ts, not finished) and encryption of extracted document text.

Things we have that DocuSign does not list: a one-time code by email; a check before sending that warns when a document likely needs a notary, a witness or a qualified signature (src/server/warnings.ts, src/lib/paperwork.ts); a public byte-for-byte /verify page and lookup by envelope ID; a dispute button ("I did not sign this"); and honest wording of what each check proves (CHECK_PROVES, CHAIN_TRUTH, MATCH_MEANS).

For the government question that comes next, the gaps in this area that most block public bodies are: (1) security certifications and authorisations (FedRAMP, ISO 27001 and national equivalents); (2) data residency per region; (3) a PKI seal on completed PDFs that Acrobat trusts (AATL); (4) organisation eSeals and EU QES through a QTSP over the open CSC API; (5) national eID or bank ID login for signers; (6) signer-held smart cards (PIV, national eID cards, via the open-source Web eID); (7) retention schedules with purge; (8) an admin security event log with SIEM export. Items 3, 7 and 8 and a basic seal can be built by us alone in days to two weeks each. Item 6 needs a native helper on the signer's computer. Items 1, 4 and 5 need contracts or audits.

inventory:send-sign.area: Sending and signing in DocuSign eSignature on every plan (fields and options, languages, SMS/WhatsApp, responsive signing, visibility, supplements, smart sections, collaborative fields, routing and workflow, envelope custom fields, correct/transfer/share/on behalf of/delegation, in-person, attachments, payments, bulk send, PowerForms/Web Forms, templates and matching, comments, reminders/expiry, focused view and embedding, mobile apps, Word/Google Docs, file types)

features.name: Core field set (signature, initial, date signed, name, email, company, title, text, number, date, checkbox, radio, dropdown, attachment, note)
features.what: The standard boxes a sender drags onto a page so each signer signs, initials and fills in data; auto-filled ones take the signer's name, email and signing date.
features.ours_evidence: FIELD_TYPES in src/server/envelopes.ts:39 = signature, initials, date_signed, full_name, email, text, number, date, company, title, checkbox, radio, dropdown, attachment, note, strike. Editor in src/components/editor/StepFields.tsx (place, drag, resize, duplicate, copy to every page). We also have a sender 'strike' field DocuSign does not list.
features.docusign_tier: Basic fields on every plan; DocuSign's plan blog lists 'interactive form fields' as a Business Pro addition
features.honesty_risk: None beyond what exists. Do not call a typed or drawn signature a 'digital signature'.

features.name: Name field variants: first name only, last name only
features.what: The Name field can print the full name, or only the first or the last name of the signer.
features.ours_evidence: Only 'full_name' exists (src/server/envelopes.ts:39, printsName at :404). No first/last split; recipients have one name column (src/server/db.ts recipients.name).
features.docusign_tier: Same field on every plan
features.honesty_risk: Splitting a name into first and last is a guess for many cultures (one-word names, family name first); let the signer correct it rather than guessing silently.

features.name: Stamp field (company seal, eHanko)
features.what: A field where the signer applies an uploaded image of a company or personal stamp, managed in their profile; an admin turns it on.
features.ours_evidence: Work in progress: src/lib/stamps.ts (STAMP_IS wording, upload limits), src/lib/stampink.ts, src/server/pdf.ts:428 mentions stamps. 'stamp' is not yet in FIELD_TYPES (src/server/envelopes.ts:39), so it cannot be placed or sent today.
features.docusign_tier: Admin must enable it in Sending Settings; plan tier not confirmed in sources
features.honesty_risk: A picture of a stamp is not a certified electronic seal (eIDAS qualified or advanced seal) and we do not check the person may use it; the code's STAMP_IS sentence already says so and must stay.

features.name: Approve and Decline fields placed on the page
features.what: Buttons on the document: Approve completes the recipient's part like signing; Decline asks for a reason and stops the envelope.
features.ours_evidence: Role 'approver' in ROLES (src/server/envelopes.ts:38) and Finish acts as approve; decline with reason via POST /sign/:token/decline (src/server/routes-sign.ts). No placeable Approve or Decline field on a page.
features.docusign_tier: Standard fields; tier not confirmed
features.honesty_risk: None special.

features.name: Envelope ID field and stamping the ID on documents
features.what: Print the envelope ID on each page (account option, permanent once applied) or as a field the sender places.
features.ours_evidence: Every page of the signed PDF carries 'Sign&Grow Envelope ID: <id>' (src/server/pdf.ts:645) and the certificate lists it (pdf.ts:360); /verify?id= looks it up. Not movable as a field and cannot be switched off.
features.docusign_tier: Account setting; tier not confirmed
features.honesty_risk: The ID proves which envelope a printout claims to be, not that the paper is unaltered; /verify already says that.

features.name: Drawing field
features.what: Lets a signer draw freehand on part of a document (a sketch, a mark on a plan).
features.ours_evidence: No drawing type in FIELD_TYPES (src/server/envelopes.ts:39). The draw pad exists only for adopting a signature (src/components/SignaturePad.tsx).
features.docusign_tier: Tier not confirmed
features.honesty_risk: A drawing is not a signature; never count it as one in the certificate.

features.name: Formula field (numbers and dates)
features.what: A read-only field calculated from other number or date fields, for totals, fees and date arithmetic.
features.ours_evidence: 'Calculate from...' on number fields: own parser in src/lib/logic.ts (+ - * /, brackets, sum(), round()), recomputed on the server in src/server/logic.ts, carried by templates, bulk and API (fields[].formula). No date arithmetic: date fields only support filled/empty rules (CONDS_FOR in src/lib/logic.ts:26).
features.docusign_tier: Business Pro ('auto-calculate values with conditional logic')
features.honesty_risk: Date arithmetic must state the time zone and calendar used; never present a computed deadline as legal advice.

features.name: Conditional fields
features.what: Show a field only when another field of the same signer has a given answer, with chained rules.
features.ours_evidence: show_when with checked, unchecked, filled, empty, equals, not_equals, more_than, less_than (CONDS in src/lib/logic.ts:15), server recompute in src/server/logic.ts, editor src/components/editor/FieldLogic.tsx, signed PDF prints only shown fields.
features.docusign_tier: Business Pro
features.honesty_risk: None beyond existing.

features.name: Text field validation masks (Email, Numbers, Letters, Date, SSN, ZIP, ZIP5-4, custom regex with own error text)
features.what: Restricts what a signer may type and shows the sender's error message when it does not match.
features.ours_evidence: Editor offers None, Email, Number, Phone only (src/components/editor/StepFields.tsx:491-493). The API also accepts a regular expression (src/server/openapi.ts:97) which the signing page compiles (problemWith in src/components/sign/fields.ts:46). No Letters, Date, postcode or national ID masks in the editor, and a regex failure shows a generic message, not the sender's own.
features.docusign_tier: Tier not confirmed
features.honesty_risk: A format check (for example a postcode or ID pattern) does not verify the value exists or belongs to the signer; say 'checked the format', never 'verified'.

features.name: Number field formatting, currency and minimum/maximum
features.what: Number fields with currency symbol, decimal places and allowed range.
features.ours_evidence: Number fields accept numbers written in many locales and currency signs (NUMBER_RULE in src/lib/numbers.ts, src/server/openapi.ts:97), stored as typed. No min, max, decimals or currency setting in the editor (StepFields.tsx).
features.docusign_tier: Tier not confirmed
features.honesty_risk: None special.

features.name: Text field options: character limit, hide text with asterisks, fixed width, tooltip
features.what: Limit how many characters a signer types, mask what they type from others viewing, keep the box from growing, and show a hover tip.
features.ours_evidence: A label shown to the signer and read by screen readers works as the tooltip (StepFields.tsx:482). Values are capped at 4,000 characters server side (fit(f.value, 4000) in src/server/envelopes.ts:313) but the sender cannot set a limit. No conceal option; no fixed-width setting.
features.docusign_tier: Tier not confirmed
features.honesty_risk: Hiding with asterisks is a screen mask, not encryption: the value is still in the database and, unless we decide otherwise, in the signed PDF. Say exactly where it is hidden.

features.name: Font family, size, colour and bold for field text
features.what: The sender chooses how entered values look on the page; admins set defaults.
features.ours_evidence: No font settings on fields (fields table in src/server/db.ts:69-74 has no font column; editor StepFields.tsx has width and height only). PDF stamping picks fonts per script (src/server/pdf.ts, README 'Scripts and fonts in the signed PDF').
features.docusign_tier: Tier not confirmed
features.honesty_risk: Any chosen font must still cover the script typed, or the existing 'printed as a visible mark' warning must apply.

features.name: Data label linking (fields with the same label share one value)
features.what: Type once, filled everywhere: several fields of one signer with the same data label take the same entry.
features.ours_evidence: 'Copy to every page' makes independent copies with new ids (copyToEveryPage in src/components/editor/StepFields.tsx:220-228); nothing links their values.
features.docusign_tier: Account data population setting; tier not confirmed
features.honesty_risk: None special.

features.name: Checkbox group validation (select at least, at most, exactly N)
features.what: Rules over a group of checkboxes, for 'tick at least one' questions.
features.ours_evidence: Radio groups exist via group_name (src/components/sign/fields.ts buildItems); checkboxes are each required or optional on their own. No group rule.
features.docusign_tier: Tier not confirmed
features.honesty_risk: None special.

features.name: Collaborative fields
features.what: A text, radio, dropdown or checkbox field that every signer may fill or change, optionally with initials required on changes.
features.ours_evidence: Every field except a note or strike belongs to exactly one recipient (error text in src/server/envelopes.ts:280-282). Formulas read another person's answer only after they finished (README 'Conditional fields and formulas').
features.docusign_tier: Tier not confirmed
features.honesty_risk: Every change must be attributed in the audit trail and, once someone has finished, trigger the existing sign-again rule; never let a later edit silently change what an earlier signer agreed to.

features.name: Sender pre-fill fields
features.what: The sender fills in text, checkboxes, radios, name or company before sending, printed into the document.
features.ours_evidence: Prefilled value and Read only for text, number, date, company, title, note, checkbox, radio, dropdown (prefilled list in src/server/envelopes.ts:294, prefill column, StepFields.tsx:483-487).
features.docusign_tier: Standard ('pre-filled fields' per plan blog)
features.honesty_risk: None beyond existing.

features.name: AutoPlace and anchor text tags (UI and API)
features.what: Put fields automatically wherever a chosen string appears, including signer-numbered tags, also for documents sent by API.
features.ours_evidence: 'Find fields for me' in the editor (StepFields.tsx:366-367) uses src/lib/autoplace.ts: existing PDF form fields, 'Signature: ____' labels, and {{signature}}, {{signature2}}, {{text:Label}} tags. It runs in the browser only (scanPdf on a pdf.js document); the API has no anchor option.
features.docusign_tier: Every plan in the web app; account-level automatic anchor tags apply to API uploads
features.honesty_risk: Found fields are suggestions; the sender must still review placement before sending.

features.name: Signature adoption: choose a style, draw, upload; saved signatures; admin limits on methods
features.what: Signers adopt a signature by style, drawing or image upload; admins can disable all but one method and lock the name.
features.ours_evidence: Tabs saved, type, draw, upload in src/components/SignaturePad.tsx:16-17; four handwriting styles for Latin names (README). No sender or admin setting to allow only one method.
features.docusign_tier: Every plan; method limits are an account setting
features.honesty_risk: Forcing 'draw' does not make a signature stronger in law; do not suggest it does.

features.name: Signing in 44 languages, sending UI in 14, per-recipient email language
features.what: The signing screen follows the signer's browser language; the sender sets a notification language per recipient; admins choose brand languages.
features.ours_evidence: LANGUAGE_NOTE in src/lib/policy.ts:223 ('The signing screen and our emails are in English for now'); <html lang="en"> in src/app/layout.tsx:30; README 'What is not in it'. All user-facing sentences are inline English strings across src/server and src/components, so extraction is large.
features.docusign_tier: Every plan
features.honesty_risk: The consent to electronic records (CONSENT_VERSION) and the 'what kind of signature this is' text are legal wording: a translation must be reviewed by a person and versioned per language; never ship machine translation of that text as final. Record in the audit trail which language version each person agreed to.
features.provider_notes: Human translators for legal text. Open tools: Weblate (self-hosted) to manage strings; LibreTranslate or Argos Translate only for first drafts of interface text. Start with the signing page, consent and emails, then the sender app.

features.name: SMS delivery of the signing link and reminders
features.what: Recipients get the signing link by text message, alone or with email.
features.ours_evidence: src/server/sms.ts (kinds code, link, reminder; recorded, retried, daily limit per account), text_link handling in src/server/signercode.ts:500-517, provider selection in src/lib/checks.ts:126-135 (Twilio or SMS_WEBHOOK_URL). Only works where the operator has set a provider.
features.docusign_tier: Multi-Channel Delivery add-on to Standard or higher; signers, CC and certified delivery only; not for signing groups, PowerForms or bulk send; up to 50 messages per envelope
features.honesty_risk: A text proves someone holds the phone, not who they are. Never say SMS was delivered when the provider only accepted it.
features.provider_notes: Twilio (paid) or any gateway behind SMS_WEBHOOK_URL. No reliable free option; open-source Android SMS gateway apps exist but are fragile. Operator sets TWILIO_ACCOUNT_SID, TWILIO_AUTH_TOKEN and TWILIO_FROM or a messaging service, and registers sender IDs where countries require it.

features.name: WhatsApp delivery of the signing link
features.what: The platform itself sends the signing invitation and reminders through WhatsApp.
features.ours_evidence: For 'I will send the link myself' recipients the envelope page has 'Share on WhatsApp' (src/components/sender/OwnLink.tsx:46), which opens the sender's own WhatsApp; src/server/bysender.ts:77,96. The server never sends a WhatsApp message.
features.docusign_tier: Same Multi-Channel Delivery add-on as SMS; cannot combine SMS and WhatsApp for one recipient
features.honesty_risk: Do not claim end-to-end encryption on our side for business messages sent through a provider, and do not claim the person read it from a 'delivered' status.
features.provider_notes: Meta WhatsApp Business Platform (Cloud API) directly, or through Twilio. Needs a verified Meta Business account, a dedicated number, pre-approved message templates, explicit opt-in, and per-message fees. No free open alternative for platform sending; the free click-to-chat link is what we already have.

features.name: Responsive signing (document reflowed to HTML on phones)
features.what: Converts the PDF or Word file to HTML so text and fields reflow to a phone screen.
features.ours_evidence: 'Text view' toggle for every signer (src/app/sign/[token]/page.tsx:1082-1106, src/components/sign/TextView.tsx) shows the document as text page by page with that signer's fields as an ordinary form; zoom 100/150/200 (src/components/sign/Zoom.tsx). The page images themselves do not reflow.
features.docusign_tier: Basic responsive signing on accounts that enable it; advanced options only on certain production plans
features.honesty_risk: The signed record is the PDF; a reflowed view must say it is a reading aid and link to the exact pages being signed, and the certificate must record which view was used.

features.name: Smart sections (collapsible sections, rotating tables, Continue buttons)
features.what: Mobile helpers inside responsive documents that hide long text until expanded and stack wide tables.
features.ours_evidence: Nothing in src/components/sign; depends on a reflowed view we do not have.
features.docusign_tier: Premium; needs responsive signing enabled
features.honesty_risk: Collapsed text is still part of what is signed; never let a signer finish without the option to read it, and do not collapse terms by default.

features.name: Document visibility per recipient
features.what: Each signer sees only the documents with their fields (plus chosen others); account-wide or set by sender per envelope.
features.ours_evidence: loadEnvelope returns every document of the envelope (src/server/envelopes.ts:89-94) and the sign routes serve any document of it (GET /sign/:token/doc/:doc in src/server/routes-sign.ts). No visibility column on documents or recipients.
features.docusign_tier: Account sending setting; tier not confirmed
features.honesty_risk: The completed copy each person gets, the evidence pack, comments and the certificate must all respect it, or we must say plainly that the final copy includes everything. Never tell a signer a document is private from others if any copy leaks it.

features.name: Supplemental documents (view, accept, must read)
features.what: Extra documents such as terms or privacy notices attached without fields, with optional rules that the signer views or accepts them.
features.ours_evidence: No such concept: every document is part of the signed set (documents table src/server/db.ts:55-58). grep for 'supplement' finds nothing in src.
features.docusign_tier: Must be enabled for the account and in the sender's permission profile
features.honesty_risk: 'Viewed' means the file was opened, not read or understood; record opened and accepted, never 'read'.

features.name: Conditional routing (conditional recipients)
features.what: Send the envelope to different recipients depending on field answers (for example amounts over a limit go to a manager).
features.ours_evidence: Routing is fixed routing_order only (src/server/envelopes.ts:244); show_when rules apply to fields of the same person, not to recipients (src/lib/logic.ts).
features.docusign_tier: Advanced Recipient Routing add-on / Advanced Workflows; DocuSign's plan blog places it in Enhanced
features.honesty_risk: Credits, daily limits and the certificate must show who was skipped and why; never present a skipped approver as having approved.

features.name: Delayed routing (wait between routing steps)
features.what: Hold the envelope for a set time between steps, for example a cooling-off period, 1 hour to 30 days.
features.ours_evidence: No delay on routing steps; advance() moves to the next routing_order at once (src/server/envelopes.ts). The timer (POST /api/cron) only handles reminders and expiry (envelopes.ts:2441).
features.docusign_tier: Enterprise Pro, or Advanced Workflow add-on for Business Pro
features.honesty_risk: A delay is not a legal cooling-off period by itself; do not label it as one.

features.name: Scheduled sending
features.what: Prepare an envelope now and have it sent automatically at a chosen date and time, up to 30 days ahead.
features.ours_evidence: No send_at or schedule column on envelopes (src/server/db.ts:44-52); POST /envelopes/:id/send sends immediately (src/server/routes-envelopes.ts).
features.docusign_tier: Standard and above
features.honesty_risk: Signatures must be reserved or checked again at send time, and a pause or daily limit at that moment must be told to the sender, not silently skipped.

features.name: Pause and resume a workflow
features.what: Hold an envelope that is out so nobody can sign and no notifications go, then resume it.
features.ours_evidence: Only the abuse pause of a whole sending account exists (README 'automatic pause'); no per-envelope pause.
features.docusign_tier: API feature; tier not confirmed
features.honesty_risk: Signers who open a paused link must be told it is paused, not that it expired.

features.name: Envelope custom fields (text or list metadata)
features.what: Admin-defined fields such as case number or cost centre that the sender fills; not shown to signers, printed on the certificate, searchable, in the API.
features.ours_evidence: No custom fields or metadata on envelopes (grep custom_field, metadata, external_id in src/server finds nothing); only folders (envelopes.folder).
features.docusign_tier: Business Pro
features.honesty_risk: Values printed on the certificate are the sender's words; mark them as such.

features.name: Document custom fields
features.what: Name/value metadata attached to an individual document in an envelope through the API.
features.ours_evidence: documents table has id, envelope_id, file_id, name, position only (src/server/db.ts:55-58).
features.docusign_tier: API; tier not confirmed
features.honesty_risk: None special.

features.name: Correct an envelope that is out
features.what: Change recipients, documents or fields of an in-progress envelope without voiding it.
features.ours_evidence: POST /envelopes/:id/correct and correctEnvelope (src/server/routes-envelopes.ts, src/server/envelopes.ts) with the 'resign' choice when finished people are affected (envelopes.ts:168, :250-251).
features.docusign_tier: Every plan
features.honesty_risk: None beyond existing.

features.name: Transfer ownership of individual envelopes and templates
features.what: A user or admin moves chosen envelopes to another user; admins run custody transfer; org admins move across accounts.
features.ours_evidence: When a member is removed, everything they sent passes to a member the admin picks (src/server/routes-trust.ts:256-264, UPDATE envelopes SET sender_id); account ownership handover at POST /account/transfer-owner (src/server/routes-account.ts:551). No per-envelope Transfer action.
features.docusign_tier: Account feature; cross-organisation transfer needs the Organization Management add-on
features.honesty_risk: The certificate and audit trail must keep the original sender; the new owner did not send it.

features.name: Shared access to envelopes (manage, edit, send) with start and end dates
features.what: A user lets a colleague view, correct, resend or send envelopes for them, with optional expiry of the access.
features.ours_evidence: Members see only their own envelopes and admins see all (src/server/routes-envelopes.ts:94; openapi.ts:174); templates are shared with the team. No per-user sharing, no levels, no dates.
features.docusign_tier: Multi-user plans; tier not confirmed
features.honesty_risk: Every action taken through shared access must name the person who did it, not the owner.

features.name: Send on behalf of another user (SOBO, act-on-behalf)
features.what: An integration or assistant sends as a named user, with the principal shown as the sender.
features.ours_evidence: An envelope's sender_id is the signed-in user or the user who created the API key (src/server/envelopes.ts createEnvelope); no principal/agent model.
features.docusign_tier: Permission profile option for API; OAuth JWT equivalent
features.honesty_risk: Show both names ('sent by A on behalf of B') to recipients and on the certificate; never hide who pressed send.

features.name: Change signing responsibility (assign to someone else) with sender control
features.what: A signer passes the request to another person; the sender or admin decides whether that is allowed; the first person becomes a copy recipient.
features.ours_evidence: reassignRecipient (src/server/envelopes.ts:1959-1994) via POST /sign/:token/reassign, with reason, audit and clearing of answers. Always allowed for signers and approvers; no envelope or account setting to switch it off; the first person is not kept as a copy recipient.
features.docusign_tier: Sender option in Advanced Options; admin default in Signing Settings
features.honesty_risk: None beyond existing.

features.name: Delegated signing (a user names a delegate for a period)
features.what: A user who will be away sets someone to sign in their place for a time window.
features.ours_evidence: No delegate settings on users; reassign is per envelope and done by the signer (envelopes.ts:1959).
features.docusign_tier: Standard ('delegated signing' per plan blog); admin must enable
features.honesty_risk: The delegate signs with their own name and signature 'for' the principal; never apply the principal's adopted signature, and never claim we know the delegate holds legal authority.

features.name: In-person signing hosted on the sender's device
features.what: An account holder hosts a signing session for someone physically present.
features.ours_evidence: Role 'inperson' (src/server/envelopes.ts:38); host session lock in src/server/handover.ts; needs a connection throughout (README).
features.docusign_tier: Standard
features.honesty_risk: The lock covers this app in that browser, not the device (IN_PERSON_LOCK in src/lib/phone.ts already says so).

features.name: Witness signing (eWitness)
features.what: A witness signs after the signer, named by the sender or by the signer.
features.ours_evidence: Role 'witness' with witness_for and named_by_signer (src/server/witness.ts, src/server/envelopes.ts:30,38).
features.docusign_tier: Business Pro ('eWitness' per plan blog). Search budget ran out before DocuSign's own witness pages could be checked.
features.honesty_risk: We record the witness's statement and cannot check presence; keep saying so.

features.name: Signer attachments
features.what: A field asking the signer to upload a supporting file, appended to the final document.
features.ours_evidence: 'attachment' field; POST /sign/:token/upload (src/server/routes-sign.ts:289-298) via storeUpload (PDF, PNG, JPEG, 25 MB); appended to the signed PDF (README 'After signing').
features.docusign_tier: Business Pro
features.honesty_risk: We do not check what an attachment is (an ID photo is not identity verification).

features.name: Payments collected during signing
features.what: A payment field charges the signer by card, bank transfer, Apple Pay or Google Pay through a connected gateway.
features.ours_evidence: Pay link only: a trusted account shows a link to its own payment page after Finish (src/server/routes-paylink.ts; README 'Reuse and scale'); we never take part in or confirm the payment.
features.docusign_tier: Business Pro or Enhanced, supported currencies and countries only
features.honesty_risk: Never mark an envelope paid unless the gateway confirmed it by webhook; never touch card data ourselves; say who the merchant is.
features.provider_notes: Stripe Connect with Checkout (each sender connects their own Stripe account, card data stays at Stripe, PCI SAQ A); PayPal; Mollie; for Africa Flutterwave, M-Pesa Daraja or Chapa. No free option; each sender needs a merchant account and pays fees.

features.name: Bulk send
features.what: Send one template to many people from a CSV list, each getting their own envelope.
features.ours_evidence: POST /bulk, /bulk/check, remind and void a batch (src/server/routes-envelopes.ts), bulk_rows for resumable sending (src/server/db.ts:113-116); up to 500 rows; a column named like a field fills it (README). DocuSign allows up to 999 rows per list.
features.docusign_tier: Business Pro and Enterprise Pro
features.honesty_risk: None beyond existing.

features.name: PowerForms (public self-service signing link)
features.what: A link anyone can open to fill and sign a template; DocuSign can cap the number of uses.
features.ours_evidence: powerforms table (src/server/db.ts:102-105), routes /powerforms and /public/powerforms/:slug/start (src/server/routes-envelopes.ts), QR codes (src/lib/qr.ts). No limit on the number of submissions.
features.docusign_tier: Business Pro or above
features.honesty_risk: The form-filler's identity is only what they typed; keep saying so.

features.name: Web Forms (mobile form first, envelope made on completion)
features.what: A responsive question-by-question form that fills a template and creates the envelope only when finished.
features.ours_evidence: PowerForms show the PDF and create the envelope at start (src/server/routes-envelopes.ts public start route); no form-first flow.
features.docusign_tier: Business Pro adds web forms; Advanced Web Forms add-on; included in IAM Professional and higher
features.honesty_risk: What is signed must be the document with the answers in it, shown before signing; the form alone is not the agreement.

features.name: Templates with roles, sharing and locked fields
features.what: Reusable documents with role placeholders, shared with the team, with control over who may change them.
features.ours_evidence: Templates with role_name, use/change rules and wording lock in src/server/tplroles.ts and src/components/templates/WhoCanUse.tsx; template_members table (README 'Reuse and scale').
features.docusign_tier: Personal has reusable templates; Standard adds shared templates
features.honesty_risk: None beyond existing.

features.name: Automatic template matching
features.what: When a file is uploaded, find saved templates whose documents look the same and offer or apply them, with a sensitivity setting.
features.ours_evidence: Nothing compares uploads with templates; text is already extracted per page at upload (extractPages in src/server/routes-envelopes.ts:67) and could be reused.
features.docusign_tier: User preference; tier not confirmed
features.honesty_risk: A match is a suggestion; the sender confirms. Never apply a template silently to a document that differs.

features.name: Several templates in one envelope (composite templates)
features.what: Apply more than one template to an envelope, combining their documents, roles and fields.
features.ours_evidence: An envelope starts from one template_id (src/server/routes-envelopes.ts:223-227).
features.docusign_tier: Tier not confirmed
features.honesty_risk: None special.

features.name: Comments (public, private, groups) with a per-envelope off switch
features.what: Senders and signers discuss the document; admins enable comments; a sender can disable them on one envelope.
features.ours_evidence: src/server/comments.ts and src/server/routes-comments.ts: whole document or page, everyone or private with the sender, limits in src/lib/policy.ts. No per-envelope switch to turn comments off (grep finds no setting).
features.docusign_tier: Standard ('real-time commenting'); off by default until an admin enables it
features.honesty_risk: None beyond existing.

features.name: Reminders and expiration with warning before expiry
features.what: Automatic reminders, expiry after N days (default 120, up to 999), warning email before expiry.
features.ours_evidence: reminder_days 0-60 and expire_days 1-365, default 120 (src/server/envelopes.ts:118, :208); DEFAULT_REMINDER_DAYS in src/lib/policy.ts; warning before deadline, extend, reopen (README). Our maximum is 365 days, DocuSign's 999.
features.docusign_tier: Every plan
features.honesty_risk: None beyond existing.

features.name: Signing order: sequential, parallel, mixed
features.what: Recipients act one after another, all at once, or in numbered steps.
features.ours_evidence: routing_order 1-99 and ordered flag (src/server/envelopes.ts:206-208, :244).
features.docusign_tier: Every plan
features.honesty_risk: None.

features.name: Recipient types: Specify Recipients (agent), Update Recipients (intermediary), Allow to Edit (editor), Needs to View (certified delivery)
features.what: Recipients who name later recipients, edit the envelope like the sender, or must view to complete it.
features.ours_evidence: ROLES = signer, approver, cc, viewer, inperson, witness (src/server/envelopes.ts:38); 'viewer' is like Needs to View; only a witness can be named by another person (named_by_signer). No agent, intermediary or editor.
features.docusign_tier: 'Review your account plan' per DocuSign docs; tier not confirmed
features.honesty_risk: Whoever named or changed a recipient must appear in the audit trail and certificate.

features.name: Signing groups
features.what: Route to a predefined group where any one member signs; members tracked in history.
features.ours_evidence: src/server/groups.ts, groups of 2 to 20 members, each with own link (README 'Signing groups'). DocuSign allows up to 50 groups of 50 members.
features.docusign_tier: Certain Enterprise plans per developer docs; Business Pro not confirmed
features.honesty_risk: None beyond existing.

features.name: Sign on paper (Print and Sign, then upload or fax)
features.what: A recipient prints, signs by hand and returns a scan; senders can allow or require it.
features.ours_evidence: Signers can view or print at any time (README) but cannot return a wet-ink scan in place of signing; no requireSignOnPaper equivalent.
features.docusign_tier: Recipient privilege, on by default per Advanced Option descriptions
features.honesty_risk: We cannot verify a scanned handwritten signature; the certificate must say 'signed on paper, scan uploaded by this link' and never treat it as an electronic signature event.

features.name: Document markup (signer edits wording, others approve)
features.what: Recipients white out or add text; every other recipient reviews the change.
features.ours_evidence: Strike-out and note are sender-only marks (SENDER_MARK in src/server/envelopes.ts:42); signers can only fix the spelling of their own name.
features.docusign_tier: Advanced Workflow module
features.honesty_risk: Any change after someone finished must use the sign-again rule.

features.name: Signing reasons (21 CFR Part 11)
features.what: The signer picks a reason for signing, required for Part 11 accounts.
features.ours_evidence: No signing_reason anywhere in src (grep).
features.docusign_tier: Part 11 module
