features.honesty_risk: A reason picker is easy; never claim 21 CFR Part 11 compliance without a validated system, re-authentication at signing and customer validation documents.

features.name: Decline with a reason, finish later, sign a document yourself
features.what: Signer actions in Other Actions; self-signing without other recipients.
features.ours_evidence: POST /sign/:token/decline and /save (src/server/routes-sign.ts), decline_reason column (src/server/db.ts:65), self-signing in src/components/editor/SendMyself.tsx.
features.docusign_tier: Every plan
features.honesty_risk: None.

features.name: Access code and private message per recipient
features.what: A code the recipient must enter, and a note only that recipient sees.
features.ours_evidence: access_code and note per recipient (src/server/envelopes.ts:244, ACCESS_CODE_MIN and ACCESS_CODE_TRIES in src/lib/policy.ts).
features.docusign_tier: Every plan
features.honesty_risk: An access code shows someone knew the code, not who they are.

features.name: Focused view and embedded signing inside an iframe
features.what: Integrators show the signing session inside their own page with a minimal wrapper, using DocuSign JS and frameAncestors.
features.ours_evidence: POST /envelopes/:id/recipient-view returns a link for redirect or a new tab; it 'cannot be shown inside an iframe' (src/server/openapi.ts:217) because next.config.mjs sets X-Frame-Options SAMEORIGIN and frame-ancestors 'self' except clickwrap pages.
features.docusign_tier: API (free developer account; production depends on API plan)
features.honesty_risk: Allow framing only for origins the account registers, never '*', and record in the audit trail that signing happened in a frame on that site, as clickwrap already does.

features.name: Embedded sending (sender view)
features.what: An integrator opens the sender's prepare-and-send screen inside their own app for a draft envelope.
features.ours_evidence: No sender-view endpoint in src/server/routes-envelopes.ts; the editor requires a logged-in session.
features.docusign_tier: API
features.honesty_risk: A one-time sender-view link is a credential; it must expire quickly and be bound to one draft.

features.name: Native mobile apps (iOS, Android)
features.what: Apps to send, sign, host in-person signing and manage envelopes.
features.ours_evidence: README 'What is not in it': native mobile apps. No manifest or service worker in public/ or src/app/layout.tsx. The web app works in phone browsers from 2023 (src/lib/mobile.ts).
features.docusign_tier: Free app for every plan
features.honesty_risk: An app store listing must not claim certifications we do not hold.
features.provider_notes: Apple Developer Program and Google Play accounts; Capacitor could wrap the web app. A PWA covers most needs without stores.

features.name: Offline signing in the mobile app
features.what: The host downloads an envelope, signs without connection (in-person), and it syncs when back online.
features.ours_evidence: README: signing without a connection is not built; opening and Finish need a connection, Finish retries by itself (src/components/sign/offline.ts).
features.docusign_tier: Mobile app feature
features.honesty_risk: Times recorded offline are the device's clock until sync; the certificate must say when the server received it and that the earlier time is device-reported.
features.provider_notes: Possible as a PWA with a service worker and IndexedDB for in-person signing only; no outside provider. Useful for field work in areas without signal.

features.name: Scan paper with the phone camera
features.what: Photograph a paper document, crop and clean it, and send it for signature.
features.ours_evidence: Several phone photos become one document, turned upright and shrunk in the browser (src/components/editor/photos.ts, PhotoAsk.tsx; storeUpload joins pictures in src/server/routes-envelopes.ts:41-62). No edge detection, perspective correction or contrast cleanup.
features.docusign_tier: Mobile app feature
features.honesty_risk: Cleaning a scan changes pixels; keep the original photo or say the image was processed.
features.provider_notes: Open source in-browser options: OpenCV.js, jscanify.

features.name: Word, Google Docs and other file types (.doc, .docx, .rtf, .txt, .htm, .xls, .ppt, .tif and more)
features.what: Upload office files directly; DocuSign converts them to PDF. Up to 25 to 50 MB per file depending on the page, 2,000 pages per document.
features.ours_evidence: storeUpload accepts only PDF, PNG, JPEG by magic bytes and says 'Export Word or Google Docs files as PDF first' (src/server/routes-envelopes.ts:49-52); 25 MB, 500 pages (:46, :64). README 'What is not in it'.
features.docusign_tier: Every plan
features.honesty_risk: Conversion can shift layout; show the converted PDF to the sender before fields are placed and state that the PDF is what is signed.
features.provider_notes: Self-hosted LibreOffice headless (free) or Gotenberg (MIT) in a sandboxed container with no network; Google Docs need the Drive export API through an OAuth app.

features.name: Cloud storage sources (Google Drive, Dropbox, Box, OneDrive)
features.what: Pick files from cloud storage when adding documents; admins choose which sources are offered.
features.ours_evidence: Upload from the device only (src/components/editor/upload.ts, POST /files). README: no ready-made integrations.
features.docusign_tier: Every plan per DocuSign's 2026 plan blog
features.honesty_risk: Request the narrowest scope (file picked by the user only) and say we do not read the rest of their drive.
features.provider_notes: Google Picker with the drive.file scope (avoids restricted-scope review), Dropbox Chooser (free), Microsoft OneDrive File Picker via Graph, Box Picker. Each needs an app registered by the operator.

features.name: Envelope size limits (recipients, documents, file size, pages)
features.what: DocuSign allows up to 99 recipients per envelope, 25 to 50 MB per file and 2,000 pages per document.
features.ours_evidence: 50 recipients, 30 documents, 2,000 fields (src/server/envelopes.ts:190-192); 25 MB per upload and 500 pages (src/server/routes-envelopes.ts:46, :64).
features.docusign_tier: Every plan
features.honesty_risk: None.

features.name: Data Verification fields (premium checks against outside databases)
features.what: Fields that check email, phone, postal address, or premium items like SSN, FEIN or bank account against trusted sources in real time.
features.ours_evidence: Only format checks (src/components/sign/fields.ts RULES).
features.docusign_tier: Depends on plan; extension apps installed by an admin
features.honesty_risk: Report exactly what the provider confirmed (for example 'address exists'), never 'identity verified'.
features.provider_notes: Country-specific address and bank validation services (paid); few open options beyond open address datasets such as OpenAddresses.

inventory:send-sign.notes: How this was researched: www.docusign.com and ecom.docusign.com could not be fetched from this session (DNS blocked by the session network allowlist), so I did not fetch any DocuSign page directly. Every DocuSign fact comes from WebSearch result summaries of the cited support.docusign.com, developers.docusign.com and docusign.com pages. To read the pages themselves, those hosts have to be allowed in the session's network settings. The web search budget for this turn (200 calls, shared by all agents) ran out before I could check DocuSign's witness and Number-field pages, so the witness tier and the Number field min/max claim rest on the plan blog and a validation-page summary only. Plan tiers often disagree between DocuSign pages: Business Pro is cited at $40 to $45, envelope allowances at 100 per user per year, and conditional routing is placed in either Enhanced or an add-on. Where a tier was not confirmed I said so. Things I left out because I found no source: a DocuSign Word add-in, and an official full list of the 44 signing languages. Code checks: I read the code read-only and wrote no files. The README matches the code for this area, with these notes. (1) The stamp field is half built (src/lib/stamps.ts, stampink.ts, pdf.ts mention it) but not yet in FIELD_TYPES. (2) The signing page's 'Text view' is our closest match to responsive signing, and the README does not call it that. (3) AutoPlace runs only in the browser editor, not through the API. (4) The embedded signing link cannot be framed. Not in my area but relevant to the user's request: README line 484 says 'Signatures never expire', which conflicts with the new rule that credits expire monthly. The biggest gaps for small organisations and public bodies, in order: languages (XL, the consent text needs human translation), Word upload (M, LibreOffice self-hosted), sign on paper (M), WhatsApp delivery (M, Meta provider), reflowed phone view (L), document visibility (M), envelope custom fields (M), scheduled sending (M), delegated signing and shared access (M each), and real payments (L, Stripe Connect or local mobile money).

inventory:iam-ai.area: DocuSign Intelligent Agreement Management and AI: Navigator, Insight, Iris, AI review and summaries, signer summaries, obligation and renewal tracking, Gen, CLM, Agreement Desk, Analyzer, search across agreements

features.name: Agreement repository that holds every completed agreement (Navigator, with completed eSignature envelopes added automatically)
features.what: One place where a team finds every signed agreement, without digging through email, with the agreement data next to each one.
features.docusign_tier: Navigator is part of the Docusign IAM plans (IAM Standard and up as we understand it), not of eSignature-only plans. Not verified in this session.
features.ours_evidence: sign-and-grow/src/server/routes-envelopes.ts:128-185 GET /envelopes lists envelopes with boxes drafts/sent/waiting/completed/closed/removed, folders and (admins) a sender filter; members see only their own (line 140), admins the whole account. /app/inbox (routes-envelopes.ts:188) lists documents sent to the signed-in person. GET /export (sign-and-grow/src/server/routes-trust.ts:134) gives a ZIP with an index.csv (envelope_id, subject, status, sent_at, completed_at, recipients, signed_pdf_sha256). What is missing: there is no agreement record beyond the envelope (sign-and-grow/src/server/db.ts:44-53 envelopes has no type, party, start, end or renewal columns).
features.honesty_risk: Do not call it a records-management or archiving system that meets a retention law. It holds what was signed here, not every agreement an organisation has.
features.provider_notes: None needed. Builds on the existing envelopes, folders, search and export.

features.name: Upload agreements signed elsewhere into the repository (bulk import of legacy PDFs)
features.what: Lets an organisation put its paper and other-tool contracts (leases, grants, supplier contracts) into the same searchable place, without sending them for signature.
features.docusign_tier: IAM plans with Navigator. Not verified in this session.
features.ours_evidence: sign-and-grow/src/server/routes-envelopes.ts:40-81 storeUpload only makes a file to send or build a template from; envelopes.kind is 'envelope' or 'template' (db.ts:46). There is no store-only record kind and no bulk upload screen.
features.honesty_risk: An imported file is not signed or verified by us: it must never get our certificate, never match on /verify as 'completed here', and its page must say 'uploaded by <person> on <date>, not signed with GrowSigning'.
features.provider_notes: None. Reuse storeUpload, the kept text for search and FILE_ENCRYPTION_KEY sealing.

features.name: AI extraction of key terms (parties, effective date, expiration date, renewal type, renewal notice period, term, total value, payment terms, governing law)
features.what: Reads each agreement and fills in its key data, so nobody has to type the dates and parties of hundreds of contracts by hand.
features.docusign_tier: IAM plans (Navigator, powered by Iris). Not verified in this session.
features.ours_evidence: Nothing extracts terms. The input exists: PDF text is read at upload (routes-envelopes.ts:68-79 extractPages, kept in files.text or sealed in files.text_sealed, sign-and-grow/src/server/searchtext.ts). No LLM is wired anywhere in src (grep for kimi, openrouter, moonshot, SUPPORT_CHAT finds nothing); the AI helper exists only as a brief (sign-and-grow/research/briefs.json key 'chat'). README 'What is not in it' says 'AI contract analysis' is not built (README.md:539).
features.honesty_risk: Never present an extracted value as correct or confirmed: show it as 'suggested by AI, check it' until a person confirms, with the quote and page it came from. Never say we 'read' or 'understand' the contract. Never send a document upstream without the account having switched document AI on, and list the host and its country on /security.
features.provider_notes: An OpenAI-compatible chat host. treegens.app uses Kimi K3 (Moonshot AI, open-weights) through OpenRouter or api.moonshot.ai (copied reference in the scratchpad treegens-chat-ref/route.ts). Document text then leaves our server, and Moonshot AI is a company based in China, which many public bodies cannot accept. Free and open option: self-host an open-weights model with vLLM, llama.cpp or Ollama; Kimi K3 itself needs a multi-GPU server, a smaller open-weights model on one GPU may be enough for dates and parties. A rules-only first pass (dates and 'between X and Y' patterns) is possible with no provider. The operator sets key, base URL and model and must add an 'ai' processor to src/lib/dataplace.ts (today only host, mail, payments, google, microsoft, sms).

features.name: Agreement type classification (NDA, MSA, SOW, lease, employment, grant and so on)

It is a warning, not a stored type, and covers only those kinds.
features.honesty_risk: A guessed type is a suggestion. Do not use it to make legal claims (for example that a document is or is not of a kind that needs a notary).

Texts kept encrypted are opened in memory for that one account (searchtext.ts sealedTextHits). Gaps: scans have no text (routes-envelopes.ts:71-76 only marks scan_pages), signer attachments are not indexed (line 68), and values typed into fields are not searched.

features.name: Obligation tracking (duties, deliverables and deadlines from agreements)

features.what: Puts signature, date and text fields in the right places without dragging each one.

features.ours_evidence: sign-and-grow/src/lib/autoplace.ts finds existing PDF form fields, labels followed by a blank ('Signature: ____') and tags like {{signature2}}; used in sign-and-grow/src/components/editor/StepFields.tsx. It is rules, not AI, and does nothing on scans.

features.name: Document generation from templates and data (eSignature document generation: Word templates with fields, conditional sections and tables filled at sending)
features.what: Makes a finished document (offer letter, volunteer agreement, grant letter) from a template and data, instead of editing a PDF by hand each time.
features.docusign_tier: Higher eSignature and IAM plans as we understand it (Professional or Enterprise level); not verified in this session.
features.ours_evidence: Fields can be prefilled by the sender (sign-and-grow/src/server/envelopes.ts:298-306), templates have roles, bulk send fills a field from a CSV column of the same name (routes-envelopes.ts:543), and fields can be conditional or calculated (sign-and-grow/src/lib/logic.ts). The wording of the document itself is never generated: no merge into text, no conditional paragraphs, no repeating rows. Word upload is not supported (routes-envelopes.ts:53; README.md:538) and README.md:539 lists document generation as not built.

features.what: Builds a quote or agreement from a Salesforce record with one click.

features.provider_notes: A Salesforce partner account and the AppExchange security review for a listed package. Charities on Salesforce Nonprofit could use our API and webhooks meanwhile.

features.name: CLM contract requests and intake forms
features.what: Staff ask for a new contract through a form (who, what, value), and it is routed to whoever drafts it.
features.docusign_tier: Docusign CLM / IAM for CLM, sales-quoted. Not verified in this session.
features.ours_evidence: PowerForms (routes-envelopes.ts:774 onward) let the public fill in and sign a template; they are not internal requests. Help tickets are for support only.
features.honesty_risk: None special.
features.provider_notes: None.

features.name: Clause library for drafting
features.what: Approved standard clauses that drafters insert, so every contract uses the agreed wording.
features.docusign_tier: Docusign CLM. Not verified in this session.
features.ours_evidence: No clause storage; documents are uploaded PDFs only.
features.honesty_risk: Clauses are the customer's; we do not vouch for them.
features.provider_notes: None. Depends on document generation.

features.name: Collaborative drafting, redlining and negotiation with the other side (tracked changes, external review)
features.what: Both sides edit and comment on the draft with tracked changes until it is agreed, then it goes for signature.
features.docusign_tier: Docusign CLM / IAM for CLM. Not verified in this session.
features.ours_evidence: Only questions and comments while an envelope is out (sign-and-grow/src/server/comments.ts, routes-comments.ts), pinned to a page or the whole document, never part of what is signed. No editing of document wording.
features.honesty_risk: Never call a comment thread a negotiated or agreed change.
features.provider_notes: An in-browser Word-compatible editor would be self-hosted ONLYOFFICE Docs (AGPL) or Collabora Online (MPL); both free to self-host, with licence duties to read first.

features.name: Version history and compare two versions
features.what: See every version of a draft and exactly what changed between them.
features.docusign_tier: Docusign CLM. Not verified in this session.
features.ours_evidence: A corrected envelope bumps content_version and keeps what changed in words (envelopes.ts:495-499, last_change), with the sign-again rule; templates keep a history of rule changes (sign-and-grow/src/server/routes-templates.ts:18); click-to-agree terms are versioned and never changed once published (db.ts:405-430). No side-by-side compare of two document versions.

features.what: Builds multi-step agreement processes (intake, approvals, signing, filing) without code.
features.docusign_tier: CLM and IAM (Maestro). Not verified in this session.

features.honesty_risk: None special.
features.provider_notes: None.

features.name: Microsoft Word add-in for drafting and sending
features.what: Work on the contract in Word and send it from there.
features.docusign_tier: Docusign CLM and eSignature add-ins. Not verified in this session.

features.honesty_risk: No 'Microsoft certified' claims.
features.provider_notes: An Office add-in is a web app plus a manifest; listing needs a Microsoft Partner Center account and AppSource validation (free), or an organisation's admin deploys the manifest.

features.name: Agreement Desk: one front door for legal requests with triage, assignment and status
features.what: A small legal or contracts team takes requests from email or forms, assigns them, tracks status and hands them to signature.
features.docusign_tier: Announced for IAM for CLM in 2025 (from Lexion) as we understand it. Not verified in this session; treat as uncertain.
features.ours_evidence: No such queue for agreements. The support ticket system (routes-support.ts, /app/operator) already has owner, priority, due times, late alerts and threads that could be adapted.
features.honesty_risk: Response times only where someone staffs the queue, as with support today.
features.provider_notes: None; AI triage would need the LLM host.

features.name: Admin switch for AI features and a written AI data-use commitment
features.what: An organisation decides whether any AI touches its documents, and knows where the text goes and that it is not used to train models.

features.ours_evidence: No AI in the code. sign-and-grow/src/lib/dataplace.ts Processor ids are host, mail, payments, google, microsoft, sms: no place to list an AI provider yet. The chat brief (research/briefs.json 'chat', point 7) plans to list the chat provider on /security.

features.provider_notes: None for the switch. The training and retention terms come from whichever host the operator picks.

inventory:iam-ai.notes:
I could not check any of this against live DocuSign pages. The web search budget for this run was already used up when I started, and WebFetch could not resolve www.docusign.com or developers.docusign.com from this session. Those two hosts would have to be allowed in the session's network settings before the facts can be checked. So every DocuSign fact, URL and plan name above comes from what I knew before this session, not from a page I read. The URLs are the canonical product, developer and pricing pages as I know them, and some paths may have moved. Check them before anything is quoted to a customer. I left out features I could not place with confidence: natural-language questions across the whole repository in Navigator, linking related agreements (an MSA to its amendments and SOWs), and AI agents announced after mid-2025. 'Obligation management' and 'Agreement Desk' are in the list but marked uncertain.

Our product (read only, nothing changed; root /home/user/treegens-app/sign-and-grow). The code matches the README on this area. README.md:539 says 'Contract lifecycle management, AI contract analysis, document generation' are not built, and the code agrees. Things worth reusing:
- Text is extracted at upload and kept, sealed when a key is set (src/server/searchtext.ts).
- Full-text search: src/server/routes-envelopes.ts:149-164.
- The timer and mail system: src/server/cron.ts and mail.ts.
- The ticket queue pattern: src/server/routes-support.ts.
- Rule-based field placement: src/lib/autoplace.ts.
- The rule-based document-kind check: src/lib/paperwork.ts.
- Field logic: src/lib/logic.ts.

The AI helper exists only as a brief (research/briefs.json key 'chat'). No LLM code is in src yet.

Every AI entry here sends document text to a model. The chat brief rules that out for the helper ('never sends a document ... upstream'). So document AI needs its own owner decision, a per-account switch that is off by default, and an 'ai' processor in src/lib/dataplace.ts so /security names the host and its country.

The open model at treegens.app is Kimi K3, reached through OpenRouter or Moonshot. Moonshot AI is based in China, which many public bodies cannot accept. Kimi K3 is open-weights, so the honest wording is 'open-weights', not 'open source'. Self-hosting it needs multi-GPU hardware. A smaller open-weights model served with vLLM, llama.cpp or Ollama on the operator's own machine is the realistic way to keep documents in one country. That matters for the government-adoption question.

Highest value for small organisations and public bodies, all buildable by us alone:
- Importing outside agreements.
- Manual key dates with a renewal dashboard and reminders.
- Pre-send approvals.
- Document generation.
- OCR.
- The admin AI switch.

AI extraction and summaries can come after, as an opt-in on top of those.

inventory:platform.area: DocuSign as a platform: eSignature REST API and SDKs, Connect webhooks, Admin API, Click API, Rooms, Maestro, Web Forms, Data Verification, App Center and extension apps, integrations, mobile apps, sandbox and go-live, API limits, embedded experiences

features.name: REST API that covers the whole product
features.what: Every action of the web app (create, send, correct, void, download, templates, recipients, bulk) can be done from the customer's own system over a JSON REST API.
features.ours_evidence: src/server/router.ts registers about 220 routes (route() table, listRoutes()); src/app/developers/page.tsx says everything the app does goes through the JSON API, same on every plan; Bearer keys in src/server/auth.ts:109.
features.honesty_risk: Do not claim parity with the DocuSign API surface; ours is smaller (no OAuth, no custom fields, no composite templates).
features.provider_notes: None.
features.docusign_tier: API plans (Starter, Intermediate, Advanced, Enterprise); tier per feature not re-verified this session

features.name: Machine-readable API description (OpenAPI)
features.what: A published OpenAPI/Swagger file that code generators and API clients (Postman, Insomnia) can import.
features.ours_evidence: src/server/openapi.ts (plus openapi-clickwrap.ts, openapi-stamps.ts) served at GET /api/openapi.json; linked from /developers.
features.honesty_risk: Keep it generated from the routes; a test should fail when a route is missing from it.
features.provider_notes: None.

features.name: Official SDKs (C#, Java, Node.js, PHP, Python, Ruby)
features.what: Client libraries in the main languages so a developer calls typed methods instead of writing HTTP by hand.
features.ours_evidence: No SDK package in the repo; only curl examples on src/app/developers/page.tsx and the OpenAPI file.
features.honesty_risk: Do not call generated clients 'official' or 'supported' unless someone maintains and versions them; publish them with the API version they match.
features.provider_notes: openapi-generator (Apache 2.0) can generate them from /api/openapi.json; publishing needs npm, PyPI, NuGet, Maven accounts (free).

features.name: Code examples, quickstarts and API explorer
features.what: Runnable example apps per language, a 'quickstart' that downloads a working project, Postman collections and an in-browser API explorer to try calls.
features.ours_evidence: src/app/developers/page.tsx has curl examples (send in three calls, correct, webhook signature check in Node). No example repos, no Postman collection, no try-it console.
features.honesty_risk: An in-browser explorer must run against a test mode, never send real emails or use signatures by accident.
features.provider_notes: Swagger UI or Redoc (open source) can render /api/openapi.json; a Postman collection can be generated from the same file.

features.name: Server-to-server API credentials
features.what: A way for a back-end system to call the API without a person present (DocuSign: integration key with JWT Grant and an RSA key pair).
features.ours_evidence: API keys tsk_ with scope send or admin (src/server/routes-account.ts POST /api-keys, src/server/auth.ts:92-122); secret stored only as SHA-256; PERSON_ONLY list in src/server/router.ts:71 blocks keys from account-control actions.
features.honesty_risk: Say plainly that a key is a bearer secret, has no expiry and skips two-step login (the developers page already does).
features.provider_notes: None. Key expiry dates and IP allowlists per key would be small additions.

features.name: OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code Grant (with PKCE) for third-party apps
features.what: Lets another company's app (a CRM, a no-code tool) ask a customer to log in and grant access to their account, with scopes and refresh tokens, instead of the customer pasting a key.
features.ours_evidence: Only Bearer API keys (src/server/auth.ts:109). src/server/oidc.ts is Google/Microsoft sign-in for people (we are the client), not an OAuth server for others.
features.honesty_risk: Consent screen must say exactly what the app can do; do not issue tokens broader than the send/admin scopes; never let an app token do PERSON_ONLY actions.
features.provider_notes: Open standard; libraries such as node-oidc-provider (MIT). Needed before listing in marketplaces like Zapier or HubSpot that expect OAuth.

features.name: Impersonation / send on behalf of another user
features.what: An admin integration sends envelopes as a named member (DocuSign JWT impersonation, 'send on behalf of'), so envelopes show the right sender without each member making a key.
features.ours_evidence: A key always acts as the user who made it (auth.ts:122 returns that user); no header or parameter to act as someone else.
features.honesty_risk: Audit trail and certificate must name both the member and the integration that acted for them; members must be able to see it.
features.provider_notes: None.

features.name: Envelope custom fields (metadata)
features.what: Text or list values attached to an envelope (case number, department, cost centre) that are searchable, returned by the API, sent in webhooks and used for reporting, without printing on the document.
features.ours_evidence: No such column on envelopes (src/server/db.ts envelopes table); grep for custom_fields/metadata/external_id in src/server finds nothing. Only folder and subject.
features.honesty_risk: State whether metadata is part of what was signed (it is not) and that it can be changed later.
features.provider_notes: None. Important for public bodies linking envelopes to case and records-management systems.

features.name: Anchor tags through the API (place fields by text in the document)
features.what: The API caller says 'put a signature 10 points right of the text /sig1/' instead of giving coordinates; works with documents generated by other systems.
features.ours_evidence: src/lib/autoplace.ts finds {{signature}} tags, 'Signature: ____' labels and PDF form widgets, but only the browser editor calls it (src/components/editor/StepFields.tsx). POST /api/envelopes needs page, x, y, w, h for every field.
features.honesty_risk: Refuse the send and name the tag when an anchor is not found, never place a field at a guessed position.
features.provider_notes: autoplace.ts already works on plain data, and files.text holds extracted text, so it can run on the server.

features.name: Composite templates
features.what: One envelope built from several server templates plus uploaded documents, with roles merged, so one standard pack (terms + order form + annex) is assembled per send.
features.ours_evidence: POST /api/envelopes takes a single template_id (src/server/routes-envelopes.ts:228, copyEnvelope); several documents per envelope are supported but not several templates.
features.honesty_risk: Locked template wording (tplroles.ts) must stay locked when combined.

features.name: Connected fields (verify any field against an outside system)

features.name: App Center marketplace
features.what: A catalogue of integrations and extension apps that customers install into their account.

features.honesty_risk: None.

features.name: Extension app platform (data write-back, file archive, file input)

features.name: Microsoft Outlook add-in

features.what: Agreements from SAP processes (procurement, HR, sales) with results written back.

features.name: Workday
features.what: Offer letters and HR forms from Workday business processes.
