inventory:platform.notes:
I could not fetch any DocuSign page in this run. The first WebSearch call came back saying the 200-search budget was already used up (every agent in this run shares it). WebFetch to developers.docusign.com and www.docusign.com then failed DNS because those hosts are outside this session's allowed network, so I stopped trying other hosts. Every DocuSign fact, number and URL above therefore comes from what I knew before this session. None was re-read today. Check them before anything public quotes them, in particular: the hourly call limit (3,000 an hour) and burst limit (500 per 30 seconds) on the rules-and-limits page, the 15-minute polling rule, the go-live rule (a set number of successful demo calls, about 20), and every plan tier (most docusign_tier values are left empty or marked "not re-verified"). Some support.docusign.com links are long document-item URLs I recall and may have moved. To verify, allow developers.docusign.com, www.docusign.com, support.docusign.com and apps.docusign.com in the network settings, or give more search budget. I left out, as unverified or belonging to other areas: Click-specific Connect events, the exact number of HMAC keys Connect allows, Connect's exact retry schedule, SMS/WhatsApp delivery (sending area), Notary and ID verification (identity area), Navigator, Iris and Agreement Desk (IAM area), payments.

Code checks that differ from the README or matter: (1) No per-key or per-account API rate limit and no rate-limit headers. The in-memory rateLimit() in src/server/util.ts covers only sign-in, public and signer routes, and it is per process. This is the most important platform gap before inviting outside integrators or public-body suppliers. (2) envelopes.test_mode exists in src/server/db.ts:460 but nothing reads it, while the docs say there is no test environment. (3) The developers page says Microsoft Teams incoming webhooks show the text property. Microsoft has been retiring Office 365 connectors in favour of Workflows, which expect Adaptive Cards, so that claim needs re-testing. (4) A webhook secret cannot be rotated without deleting the webhook. (5) recipient-view returns the long-lived signing link, framing is refused (X-Frame-Options SAMEORIGIN), and there is no return URL. (6) Autoplace tags work only in the browser editor, not through the API. Our extras that DocuSign does not document in the same way: Idempotency-Key on create and bulk, the same API on every plan, and a webhook delivery log with redelivery.

For the government goal, these platform items carry the most weight. SAML or Entra SSO plus SCIM. Microsoft 365 links: SharePoint archive, Power Automate, Teams, the Word and Outlook add-ins. Envelope custom fields so documents can be filed against case numbers. Webhooks that carry documents, with mTLS. A sandbox or test-mode key for suppliers. n8n or Power Automate recipes instead of a marketplace. Cheapest wins by value per size: per-key rate limits (S), envelope-level webhooks, more events and secret rotation (S each), return URL (S), the status-changes-since filter (S), prefilled fields on POST /envelopes with template_id (S), envelope custom fields (M), test-mode keys (M), and a check against the Companies House or Charity Commission register (M, free APIs). No files were changed in /home/user/treegens-app/sign-and-grow, and I used no scratch files.

inventory:admin.area: Administration and teams: organisation admin, users, groups, permission profiles, SSO (SAML 2.0), SCIM, domain claiming, brands and resource files, reports, exports, envelope sharing, activity logs, retention, account security settings, billing and usage

features.name: Organisation over several accounts
features.what: One organisation links several eSignature accounts (for example the departments of a council or the branches of a charity). Organisation admins see and manage every user and account in one place and can hand admin rights to others.
features.ours_evidence: Accounts stand alone: src/server/db.ts has accounts and memberships tables and nothing that groups accounts. A person can belong to several accounts, but every admin route acts on the one account of the session (c.account in src/server/routes-account.ts, PATCH /account, /account/members). The only cross-account role is the platform operator (OPERATOR_EMAILS, /app/operator), which is the server's staff, not a customer's admin.
features.docusign_tier: DocuSign Admin organisation features, enhanced (enterprise) plans as recalled; verify on the live plan comparison
features.honesty_risk: Do not call it equivalent to DocuSign Org Admin or promise delegated-admin granularity that the server does not enforce on every route and API key. An organisation admin must never be able to open a member's own private workspace outside the organisation.
features.provider_notes: No outside service. New organisation table, organisation admins, a link between accounts, and an organisation-wide user list.

features.name: Users in several accounts, switching between them
features.what: One login can belong to several accounts and switch between them without signing out.
features.ours_evidence: memberships table (src/server/db.ts:26), POST /auth/switch (src/server/routes-account.ts:287), GET /me returns every account with its role (routes-account.ts:319), users.last_account_id opens the last workspace. billingState warns about other paid plans the person manages (src/server/routes-billing.ts:521).
features.docusign_tier: All multi-user plans
features.honesty_risk: None beyond what exists.
features.provider_notes: None.

features.name: Invite users, admin and member roles, change roles, remove users
features.what: Admins invite people by email, give them a role, change it later and remove them. DocuSign does this per account with permission profiles and in DocuSign Admin.
features.ours_evidence: Owner, admin and member roles. POST /account/invites, PATCH and DELETE /account/members/:id, POST /account/leave, POST /account/transfer-owner (src/server/routes-account.ts:426-584). Removal hands envelopes, templates and bulk sends to a chosen successor (handOver in src/server/routes-trust.ts), stops the person's API keys and emails the admins. Invitations follow the anti-abuse rules and a daily limit until the account is trusted (inviteRefusal, src/server/envelopes.ts:1105). Team tab in src/app/app/settings/page.tsx (function Team).
features.docusign_tier: Standard and up (multi-user plans)
features.honesty_risk: None beyond what exists.
features.provider_notes: None.

features.name: Close and reactivate a user
features.what: An admin closes a user (no sign-in, keys stop) and can reactivate them later with everything intact, for staff on leave or contractors between jobs.
features.ours_evidence: Only removal exists: DELETE /account/members/:id deletes the membership row and hands over what they sent (routes-account.ts:474-525). memberships has no suspended or closed state (src/server/db.ts:26-30 and the added columns).
features.docusign_tier: All multi-user plans
features.honesty_risk: A closed user's sessions and API keys must stop at once, as removal does now; envelopes out for signature in their name must carry on and the screens must say who now answers for them.
features.provider_notes: None.

features.name: Bulk user import, update and export (CSV)
features.what: Admins add or change many users at once from a CSV file and download the user list, instead of one invitation at a time.
features.ours_evidence: Invitations are one at a time (POST /account/invites, routes-account.ts:426). GET /account/members returns JSON for the screen; there is no CSV export of members and no bulk import route.
features.docusign_tier: DocuSign Admin bulk actions, organisation plans as recalled
features.honesty_risk: Each invitation is an email under the same anti-abuse rules and daily limit (TEAM_INVITES_PER_DAY) until an account is trusted; do not promise that hundreds of people are provisioned at once. Say how many go today and when the rest go.
features.provider_notes: None. Export is S on its own; import with validation and a dry run is the M part.

features.name: Permission profiles (custom roles)
features.what: Named sets of permissions given to users: DocuSign ships DS Admin, DS Sender and DS Viewer and lets admins make their own, switching on or off sending, bulk send, templates, PowerForms, signing groups, viewing account reports and more.
features.ours_evidence: Three fixed roles. The router knows only the levels user, admin and public (src/server/router.ts:25 and :133). Every member can send, bulk send and use templates; there is no view-only or approve-only role and no per-permission switch. The only finer rules are per template (who may use or change it, src/server/tplroles.ts) and per API key (send or admin scope, router.ts:96-140).
features.docusign_tier: Multi-user plans; custom profiles on higher tiers as recalled, verify
features.honesty_risk: Only claim a permission where the server refuses the call, not where a screen hides a button. API keys must never carry more than their creator's profile. A read-only auditor role must not see private comment threads it is not in.
features.provider_notes: None. The work is enforcing each permission in every route, bulk send, PowerForms, templates and the API.

features.name: User groups (for sharing templates, brands and permissions)
features.what: Admins put users in groups and share templates with a group, give a group its own brand, and assign permissions through it.
features.ours_evidence: No user groups. A template can be limited to chosen individual members (template_members table, src/server/tplroles.ts, GET and PUT /api/envelopes/:id/access). Signing groups exist but are groups of recipients, not of team members (src/server/groups.ts).
features.docusign_tier: Multi-user plans as recalled
features.honesty_risk: Group changes must apply with the same care as the template rules today (history lines, removal on leaving), or a person who left a group keeps access.
features.provider_notes: None.

features.name: Signing groups
features.what: A recipient that is a group of people, any one of whom can sign for it, kept by admins.
features.ours_evidence: src/server/groups.ts and src/server/routes-groups.ts (GET /groups for everyone, POST, PUT, DELETE for admins), signing_groups and signing_group_members tables, tests/groups.test.ts, Contacts page. Each member gets their own link; the certificate names who acted for the group.
features.docusign_tier: Business Pro and up as recalled
features.honesty_risk: None beyond what exists.
features.provider_notes: None.

features.name: Single sign-on with SAML 2.0 and a login policy
features.what: Staff sign in through the organisation's own identity provider (Entra ID, Okta, Google Workspace and so on). Admins can require SSO, allow passwords as well, and create users on first sign-in (just in time).
features.ours_evidence: src/app/security/page.tsx:163-164 says plainly there is no SAML and a team cannot make its members sign in one way. Google and Microsoft OpenID Connect sign-in exist for anyone (src/server/oidc.ts). MICROSOFT_TENANT in .env.example can limit Microsoft sign-in to one organisation, but for the whole server, not per team, and passwords cannot be switched off for a team. README 'What is not in it' lists SSO as not built.
features.docusign_tier: Enhanced (enterprise) plans or the access management add-on, as recalled; verify
features.honesty_risk: SSO shows which staff member signed in to send; it says nothing about who a recipient is and does not raise the level of any signature. Do not claim support for an identity provider that was not tested. SAML needs defences against XML signature wrapping and replay, and an outside security review before it is called safe.
features.provider_notes: No paid provider. SAML 2.0 is an open standard and open-source service provider libraries exist (node-saml, samlify). The customer brings their identity provider; test against Keycloak (free, open source) and the free tier of Entra ID. Per-team OpenID Connect could reuse src/server/oidc.ts and is a smaller first step (M). Enforcing SSO for a team should wait for domain claiming so it cannot shut out people outside the domain.

features.name: Domain claiming
features.what: An organisation proves it owns an email domain by adding a DNS TXT record. Users with addresses on a claimed domain can then be managed by the organisation, and SSO can be required for them.
features.ours_evidence: No domain table or DNS check anywhere in src. src/server/oidc.ts:149-173 reads Google's hd claim and Microsoft's xms_edov only to decide whether a provider vouches for one address.
features.docusign_tier: DocuSign Admin organisation features, enhanced plans as recalled
features.honesty_risk: Claiming a domain must never silently take over someone's existing login, their own workspace or documents sent to them: the person is told first and only their sign-in rules change (the care in src/server/reclaim.ts is the model). A claimed domain does not verify signers.
features.provider_notes: DNS TXT lookup with node:dns, no outside service. Needs periodic re-checks and a way to release a domain.

features.name: SCIM 2.0 user provisioning
features.what: The organisation's identity provider creates, updates and deactivates users automatically, so a leaver loses access the day they leave.
features.ours_evidence: No /scim routes and no provisioning tokens; members only arrive by invitation (routes-account.ts:426).
features.docusign_tier: Enhanced (enterprise) plans as recalled
features.honesty_risk: Do not say we are in the Entra or Okta app galleries until a listing is accepted. Deprovisioning must hand over envelopes and stop keys exactly as removal does now, never delete signed documents.
features.provider_notes: Open standard (RFC 7643, RFC 7644); the customer's identity provider is the client. Gallery listings (Okta Integration Network, Microsoft Entra app gallery) are free but reviewed; a custom non-gallery app works without them.

features.name: Brand: logo and colour on emails, signing screen and public forms
features.what: The account's logo and colour appear in emails to recipients and on the signing screen.
features.ours_evidence: accounts.brand_color and brand_logo (src/server/db.ts:22), saved by PATCH /account with checks (src/server/routes-account.ts:402-419), Settings, Account tab. Used in emails (src/server/mail.ts:75-78), the signing screen bar with readable text colour (src/components/sign/parts.tsx:38-81) and public forms (src/app/f/[slug]/page.tsx).
features.docusign_tier: Standard: customized branding, as recalled
features.honesty_risk: None beyond what exists.
features.provider_notes: None.

features.name: Several brands, chosen per envelope, template or group
features.what: An account keeps several brands (names, logos, colours) and picks one when sending, or gives one to a group, with default brands for sending and signing.
features.ours_evidence: One brand only, stored as two columns on the accounts row (src/server/db.ts:22); envelopes have no brand reference.
features.docusign_tier: Higher tiers as recalled (multiple brands); verify
features.honesty_risk: Every brand name must pass the same well-known-brand check as the account name (nameRefusal in PATCH /account) or brands become a phishing tool. Emails and the signing screen must still name the platform and link to /check.
features.provider_notes: None.

features.name: Full brand colour set and extra logos
features.what: Separate colours for header background, header text and buttons, and separate logos for the signing screen and emails.
features.ours_evidence: One colour and one logo. The text colour on the bar is worked out for readability (inkOn in src/components/sign/parts.tsx:38).
features.docusign_tier: Branding plans as recalled
features.honesty_risk: Keep contrast at WCAG AA; refuse colour pairs that are not readable.
features.provider_notes: None.

features.name: Custom email wording per notification
features.what: The account or brand sets its own wording for each kind of email (signing request, reminder, completed, declined), with company links in the footer.
features.ours_evidence: Only a subject and message per envelope (envelopes.subject, envelopes.message in src/server/db.ts:47). Every email's wording is fixed in the code (src/server/mail.ts and callers in src/server/envelopes.ts).
features.docusign_tier: Branding resource files, higher tiers as recalled
features.honesty_risk: The fake-notice filter (src/server/fakenotice.ts) must read the custom wording. The security lines (the security code, the /check link, how to report) must stay and cannot be edited out.
features.provider_notes: None.

features.name: Signing and sending resource files
features.what: DocuSign lets admins download and upload XML resource files that replace the text of the signing and sending screens and emails.
features.ours_evidence: No mechanism to override screen text; wording lives in components and src/lib/policy.ts.
features.docusign_tier: Higher tiers as recalled
features.honesty_risk: Free editing of screen text could remove the consent statements, the decline and report options or the warnings that protect signers. If anything, offer a short list of safe text fields instead (S to M).
features.provider_notes: None.

features.name: Destination URLs after signing, declining or timing out, and a return URL for embedded signing
features.what: After a signer finishes, declines or their session ends, they are sent to a page the sender chooses, for example back to the council's website.
features.ours_evidence: POST /envelopes/{id}/recipient-view takes no return address (src/server/openapi.ts:222); no redirect setting on accounts or envelopes. The only link after Finish is the sender's payment link (src/server/routes-paylink.ts).
features.docusign_tier: Branding and embedded signing, as recalled
features.honesty_risk: Only https public addresses, with the checks the payment link already uses (no IP, port or this server). Never leave the finish screen before the signer has seen that signing is done and how to get their copy.
features.provider_notes: None.

features.name: The account's own electronic record and signature disclosure
features.what: An account replaces the standard consent text shown before signing with its own legal wording.
features.ours_evidence: One versioned wording for everyone: CONSENT_VERSION and consentWording in src/lib/policy.ts:193-210; the audit trail records the version each person agreed to.
features.docusign_tier: Account admin setting, as recalled
features.honesty_risk: Custom text may add to the core statements, never remove them (a simple electronic signature, rules differ by country and document, some documents need more). It must never say the signature equals a handwritten or qualified one. Each custom version must be stored and recorded per signer like today.
features.provider_notes: None.

features.name: Account-wide sending and signing settings
features.what: Admins decide what senders and signers may do across the account: defaults for reminders and expiry, whether senders may change them, which signature styles are allowed, and other sending and signing switches.
features.ours_evidence: Admins set the defaults for reminders, deadline and date format (PATCH /account, routes-account.ts:402-419; Settings, Account tab in src/app/app/settings/page.tsx:188-222), but every sender can change them per envelope and there are no switches for signature styles, in-person signing, bulk send and the like.
features.docusign_tier: Account admin settings, all admin plans
features.honesty_risk: Do not offer switches that take away signers' protections: decline, 'I did not sign this', report, view and print.
features.provider_notes: None.

features.name: Regional settings (default time zone and language)
features.what: Account defaults for time zone, date and time format and language.
features.ours_evidence: Default date format per account (accounts.default_date_format, routes-account.ts:412-414). Time zone comes from each browser (users.tz, routes-account.ts:303-309). English only (LANGUAGE_NOTE in src/lib/policy.ts:223).
features.docusign_tier: All plans
features.honesty_risk: Translations of the consent text and legal notices need native-speaker review before they are offered.
features.provider_notes: A default time zone is S; languages are the L part and belong with the localisation work.

features.name: Reports dashboard
features.what: Standard reports on envelopes: how many sent, completed, declined, voided, how long completion takes, activity over time and by sender.
features.ours_evidence: GET /reports/summary (src/server/routes-account.ts:699-710) and src/app/app/reports/page.tsx: counts by status, completion rate, average time to complete, the last 12 months, and per team member for admins; members see their own. The API reaches it with a send key.
features.docusign_tier: Standard and up as recalled
features.honesty_risk: None beyond what exists.
features.provider_notes: None.

features.name: Custom reports with filters and date ranges, downloaded as CSV
features.what: Admins choose the date range, status, sender, template and columns, save the report and download it as a spreadsheet.
features.ours_evidence: /reports/summary has no date range, filters or CSV (routes-account.ts:699-710). The account export ZIP carries envelopes.csv with one row per envelope (src/server/routes-trust.ts:144 and :182), click-to-agree acceptances export as CSV (src/server/routes-clickwrap.ts:224), and the envelope list filters by box, folder and search (src/server/routes-envelopes.ts:139-184).
features.docusign_tier: Higher tiers for advanced reporting as recalled; verify
features.honesty_risk: Numbers must match the lists they link to (the rule stated at routes-account.ts:700) and say what is left out, such as envelopes their sender deleted.
features.provider_notes: None.

features.name: Envelope custom fields (account-defined metadata)
features.what: Admins define fields such as case number, cost centre or department that senders fill in on each envelope, used for search and reports.
features.ours_evidence: Envelopes carry subject, message and folder only (src/server/db.ts:44-52 and added columns); search looks at those, people and document text (routes-envelopes.ts:150-160).
features.docusign_tier: Business Pro and up as recalled; verify
features.honesty_risk: Metadata is not part of what was signed unless it is printed on the document; screens and the certificate must say which it is.
features.provider_notes: None.

features.name: Export envelopes, certificates and audit trails in bulk
features.what: Download signed documents, certificates of completion and envelope histories, for many envelopes at once or one at a time.
features.ours_evidence: GET /export (src/server/routes-trust.ts:134-201): one ZIP with signed PDFs and certificates, each audit trail as JSON, comments, envelopes.csv and a README, filtered by ids or bulk batch, all senders for admins, free on every plan. GET /api/envelopes/:id/evidence gives the evidence pack (src/server/routes-evidence.ts). No date-range filter on the export.
features.docusign_tier: All plans
features.honesty_risk: None beyond what exists.
features.provider_notes: None.

features.name: Activity monitoring and an account audit log (DocuSign Monitor)
features.what: A log of what users and admins did across the account (sign-ins, role and settings changes, keys created, envelopes deleted), with dashboards, alerts on unusual activity and an API to feed a security monitoring system.
features.ours_evidence: Per envelope: hash-chained audit trail (audit table, src/lib/evidence.ts). Per person: browsers signed in (GET /me/sessions, routes-account.ts:372) and the two-step history (two_step_log, src/server/db.ts:385). Template history (tplroles.ts) and the webhook delivery log. No account-wide log of admin actions or sign-ins that an admin can read or export; billing_log (db.ts:159) is internal.
features.docusign_tier: Paid add-on (Monitor), as recalled
features.honesty_risk: Unless it is built hash-chained like the envelope trail, do not call it tamper-evident. Do not claim threat or anomaly detection we do not have; simple rule-based alerts are what they are. The log of sign-ins holds personal data and needs its own retention period in the processing summary.
features.provider_notes: None for the log and CSV/API export (M). Alerts and dashboards make it L.

features.name: Shared Access to envelopes and shared envelope folders
features.what: A user shares their envelopes (view or manage) with a colleague, for example cover during leave, and shared envelopes show up for that colleague.
features.ours_evidence: Members see only what they sent and its folders; admins see everything (src/server/routes-envelopes.ts:139-176, src/server/openapi.ts:179). Template folders belong to the team, envelope folders to their sender. The envelope page's error says 'Ask them to share it' (src/app/app/envelopes/[id]/page.tsx:60), but no sharing exists.
features.docusign_tier: Standard and up as recalled
features.honesty_risk: Fix the 'Ask them to share it' wording now, because it promises a feature that is not there. Private comment threads stay private to the person and the sender's side; each action by the person shared with goes into the audit trail under their own name.
features.provider_notes: None.

features.name: Envelope transfer between users (rules and bulk transfer)
features.what: Admins move chosen envelopes from one user to another, or set standing rules that pass envelopes on, without removing anyone.
features.ours_evidence: Envelopes, templates and bulk sends pass automatically only when someone leaves or is removed (handOver in src/server/routes-trust.ts, called from routes-account.ts:497 and :547), with an audit line. No transfer while both people stay, and no standing rules.
features.docusign_tier: Higher tiers as recalled; verify
features.honesty_risk: Each audit trail must say who handed it to whom, as handOver already does; recipients' links and the sender name on emails already out must be handled and stated.
features.provider_notes: None.

features.name: Document retention and purge
features.what: An account-wide rule that removes documents from completed or voided envelopes after a set number of days, with a choice to keep the certificate and data or remove those too, and a purge for one envelope.
features.ours_evidence: A signed envelope is kept until the account is deleted (src/app/security/processing/page.tsx:59-61). Deleting only hides it from the sender (envelopes.hidden_at), and an admin can put it back (POST /envelopes/:id/restore, src/server/routes-envelopes.ts:375). No timed purge, no 'documents only' purge, no redaction. The same page says the account holder decides how long documents are kept (processing/page.tsx:41), which overstates today's control.
features.docusign_tier: Enhanced plans as recalled; verify
features.honesty_risk: Say what stays after a purge: copies already emailed to recipients, the fingerprint kept for /verify, and backups the operator keeps. Recipients must be told their link ends. Never purge an envelope that is disputed. Do not call it records-management compliant.
features.provider_notes: None. A legal hold that blocks the purge is a small addition once retention exists (see notes).

features.name: Password rules
features.what: Admins set password length and complexity, expiry, history and lockout after failed sign-ins.
features.ours_evidence: Fixed rules: at least 8 characters (src/server/routes-account.ts:91, :261, :355), scrypt hashing (src/server/auth.ts:13-15), sign-in limited to 10 tries in 15 minutes per address and 30 per internet address (routes-account.ts:133-134). Nothing an admin can set.
features.docusign_tier: All admin plans
features.honesty_risk: NIST SP 800-63B advises against forced expiry and composition rules; offer longer minimums, a breached-password check and lockout, and do not claim compliance with any named standard.
features.provider_notes: A breached-password check can use the free k-anonymity range API of Have I Been Pwned or a downloaded list, so no password leaves the server.

features.name: Session timeout
features.what: Admins choose how long a signed-in browser stays signed in, including after a period of inactivity.
features.ours_evidence: Fixed: signed out 30 days after signing in however often used (SESSION_DAYS and SESSION_MAX_DAYS in src/lib/policy.ts:360-367, sessionEnd in src/server/auth.ts:11). People can sign out other browsers (POST /me/sessions/sign-out-others, routes-account.ts:381), and hosting in-person signing locks the browser (src/server/handover.ts). No admin-set or idle timeout.
features.docusign_tier: Account security settings, as recalled; verify
features.honesty_risk: An idle timeout only counts if the server enforces it; a timer in the page alone must not be described as a security control.
features.provider_notes: None.

features.name: Plan and billing management
features.what: See the plan, pay, update the card, download invoices and receipts, see billing history, upgrade or cancel.
features.ours_evidence: Plan tab and src/server/routes-billing.ts: GET /billing (634), checkout (708), top-up (736), provider portal for card and invoices (931), cancel (975), resume (977), self-serve refund (1008), remove card (1046), stop from an email link or with the card (1062-1134). Payments listed with receipt or invoice links (523-526); tax ID and billing address collected at checkout (775). Free plan codes for communities (FREE_PLAN_CODES).
features.docusign_tier: All self-serve plans
features.honesty_risk: This is pay per signature, not per seat; any comparison with DocuSign prices must say so.
features.provider_notes: Stripe, already integrated; the operator sets the keys.

features.name: Annual billing and paying by invoice or purchase order
features.what: Pay once a year, or receive an invoice and pay by bank transfer against a purchase order, as public bodies and larger charities usually must.
features.ours_evidence: Month to month by card only (README 'Paying'; routes-billing.ts checkout through the provider's hosted page). No send-invoice flow, no bank transfer, no purchase order number on invoices.
features.docusign_tier: Annual billing on self-serve plans; contracts and invoicing through sales on enhanced plans, as recalled
features.honesty_risk: Do not claim public-sector e-invoicing compliance (for example Peppol) unless it is done through an accredited access point. If credits start to expire each month, an annual prepaid plan needs a written rule for what expires when.
features.provider_notes: Stripe Invoicing (send_invoice with bank transfer) covers invoices and purchase order references with the existing provider; the operator switches it on. Peppol delivery needs a certified access point (a paid contract; open-source software exists but the operator still needs OpenPeppol accreditation or a provider).

features.name: Usage reports (envelopes or signatures used per period and per user)
features.what: See how much of the allowance is used, by month and by user, and download it.
features.ours_evidence: Plan page shows balance, held and available signatures (creditSummary, src/server/credits.ts:109-113) and the last 40 ledger lines (routes-billing.ts:528). Reports show sends per member. No usage by month or by user, no download.
features.docusign_tier: All plans
features.honesty_risk: If credits are changed to expire each month (as requested), the usage report must show what expired and when, and the statements 'Signatures never expire' in the README and src/server/credits.ts:7 must change in the same release, along with the refund order in paidAvailable.
features.provider_notes: None.

inventory:admin.notes:
How the DocuSign side was gathered: in this run no DocuSign page could be read. The first WebSearch call came back with 'web search budget used up' (a limit shared by every agent in the workflow run), and WebFetch could not resolve www.docusign.com or developers.docusign.com because the sandbox network does not allow those hosts. So the DocuSign features, tiers and URLs above come from what I already knew of DocuSign's public developer reference and product pages. None was checked today. The URLs are where I know these facts are published. The paths I am least sure of are envelopetransferrules, the billing category page and the Monitor product page. Tiers are marked 'as recalled' and must be checked against the live plan comparison before anyone quotes them. To check them, allow the docusign.com hosts in the session's network settings, or run a follow-up with search budget left.

Left out because I could not tie them to a DocuSign source: an IP allow list for user sign-in (what I know DocuSign publishes is its own IP ranges for customers' firewalls), legal hold in eSignature, scheduled report emails, and an owner-required two-step login. Two notes on these. We already have the two-step requirement: the owner can require it and admins can reset a member (src/server/routes-twostep.ts:351-409). Legal hold is still worth building next to retention for public bodies (FOI and litigation). It is S once retention exists: a flag that blocks purge and deletion, shown on the envelope, with a line in the audit trail.

Honesty problems found in our code now, worth fixing whatever else is built:
1. src/app/app/envelopes/[id]/page.tsx:60 tells a member to 'Ask them to share it', but envelopes cannot be shared.
2. src/app/security/processing/page.tsx:41 says the account holder decides how long documents are kept. In fact a signed envelope can only be removed by deleting the whole account (same page, lines 59-61).

The user wants credits to expire monthly 'like Claude'. That contradicts 'Signatures never expire' in README 'Paying' and src/server/credits.ts:7, and it changes the refund maths in paidAvailable (credits.ts:115-134). It touches usage reports and plan management in this area.

For government adoption, the gaps in this area that matter most are: SSO with SAML (or per-organisation OIDC first), then domain claiming, SCIM deprovisioning, permission profiles with a read-only auditor role, an exportable account audit log, retention with legal hold, configurable session timeout, and invoice or purchase-order billing. Some of this is partly covered for a public body that runs its own server: MICROSOFT_TENANT can limit Microsoft sign-in to its tenant, and OPERATOR_EMAILS gives it the operator queue. But neither works per team on a shared server.

Our product also does things in this area that I could not match to anything on DocuSign's side: an admin restore of envelopes a sender removed, handover with stopped-key notices when someone leaves, and an export that keeps working after a plan ends. I changed no files in /home/user/treegens-app/sign-and-grow. /tmp/gap-admin is empty.

added.name: Own Electronic Record and Signature Disclosure per account and per language, with withdrawal of consent
added.what: The account replaces the platform's consent text with its own disclosure (company name and phone, how to get a paper copy and what it costs, how to withdraw consent by email, post or phone and what withdrawing means), one version per language, shown once per account, per envelope or at every access. A signer who declines can also withdraw consent.
added.ours_evidence: One fixed, versioned wording for everyone: CONSENT_WORDINGS and CONSENT_VERSION '2026-11' in src/lib/policy.ts:196-207, recorded per signer (consentAuditNote). It says the signer may ask the sender for a paper copy, but no account can change the text, there is one language, nothing states a withdrawal procedure, a fee or the hardware and software needed, and grep for 'withdraw' finds nothing in the signing flow (only billing and two-step code).
added.docusign_tier: Account setting and API (/consumer_disclosure/{langCode}, consumerDisclosure.withdrawByEmail/withdrawByMail/withdrawByPhone/withdrawConsequences/copyCostPerPage, accountSettingsInformation.allowCDWithdraw, consumerDisclosureFrequency); plan tier not confirmed
added.honesty_risk: For US consumers the ESIGN Act section 101(c) lists what such a disclosure must say; do not call our default text an ESIGN consumer disclosure. Keep our own sentence on what kind of signature this is next to the account's text, record which version and language each person agreed to, and have translations reviewed by a person.
added.provider_notes: None. Public bodies usually have their own legal wording and must be able to use it.

added.name: BCC email archive
added.what: An admin sets one or more archive addresses that receive a blind copy of every envelope email of the account, for records management and freedom-of-information capture; the copy can carry a dummy link instead of the live signing link.
added.ours_evidence: No BCC anywhere in src/server/mail.ts or src/server/envelopes.ts (grep). Emails are kept in the emails table for MAIL_COPY_DAYS (90) and appear in the export and evidence pack, but nothing is copied to an archive mailbox.
added.docusign_tier: Account setting and API (/settings/bcc_email_archives, accountSettingsInformation.bccEmailArchive, enableBccDummyLink); plan tier not confirmed
added.honesty_risk: A live signing link or security code in an archive mailbox lets anyone who reads the archive sign; send the archive copy with the link and code removed, as the evidence pack already does, and say so.
added.provider_notes: None beyond the existing SMTP relay.

added.name: Watermark on documents while they are in process
added.what: An account setting puts a chosen text watermark (font, size, colour, angle, transparency, localised) across documents until the envelope is completed.
added.ours_evidence: Only copies of envelopes that were voided, declined or ran out of time get a notice page and a large stamp across every page (withNotice, renderEnvelopePdf opts.notice and drawStamp in src/server/pdf.ts:589-653). No watermark on a document still out for signing and no account setting.
added.docusign_tier: Account setting (waterMarkEnabled, showLocalizedWatermarks, /watermark preview); plan tier not confirmed
added.honesty_risk: A watermark marks a copy as unfinished; it does not stop copying or printing.

added.name: Account password rules
added.what: Admins set minimum length, required character kinds, minimum age, expiry, lockout after failed tries and lockout duration for the account's users.
added.ours_evidence: One fixed rule: at least 8 characters (src/server/routes-account.ts:91, :261, :355). Two-step login with an authenticator app exists (src/server/twostep.ts), but an admin cannot require stronger passwords or two-step for the team from a password policy.
added.docusign_tier: Account setting and API (/settings/password_rules: minimumPasswordLength, passwordIncludeDigit, expirePasswordDays, lockoutDurationMinutes, questionsRequired); plan tier not confirmed
added.honesty_risk: NIST SP 800-63B advises against forced periodic expiry and composition rules; offer a minimum length, a breached-password check and required two-step instead, and do not claim a password policy meets any named baseline.
added.provider_notes: Pwned Passwords range API (free, k-anonymity) for the breach check.

added.name: Idle session timeout and one session at a time
added.what: Admins set how many idle minutes (20 to 120) log a user out, a separate idle timeout for signing sessions and for mobile, and can forbid being logged in in several sessions at once.
added.ours_evidence: SESSION_DAYS = 30 since last use and SESSION_MAX_DAYS = 30 since sign-in (src/lib/policy.ts:360-367, src/server/auth.ts); Settings, Profile lists and signs out browsers. No idle timeout in minutes, no account setting, signing pages have no idle timeout, and signing in elsewhere signs nothing out (README 'Team and admin').
added.docusign_tier: Account settings sessionTimeout, signingSessionTimeout, mobileSessionTimeout, disableMultipleSessions; plan tier not confirmed
added.honesty_risk: An idle timeout protects an unattended screen, not a stolen cookie; say what it does.
added.provider_notes: None. Government security baselines commonly ask for a session lock after a short idle period.

added.name: Permission profiles and user groups
added.what: Admins define named permission profiles (what a user may send, see, change, administer) beyond the built-in ones, put users in groups, and assign profiles, brands and template sharing per group.
added.ours_evidence: Three fixed roles owner, admin and member (memberships table, src/server/db.ts:26; routes PATCH /account/members/:id in src/server/routes-account.ts:466); API key scopes send and admin; templates can be limited to chosen members one person at a time (template_members, src/server/tplroles.ts). No custom profiles and no user groups (signing groups are recipients, not users).
added.docusign_tier: API (/permission_profiles, /groups, /groups/{groupId}/users, /groups/{groupId}/brands); plan tier not confirmed
added.honesty_risk: Every change of a person's rights must be in an admin-visible log.

added.name: Organisation single sign-on, claimed domains and externally managed users
added.what: Users of an organisation sign in through its identity provider, the organisation claims its email domains, and the account can require that users are created and removed only by the external directory.
added.ours_evidence: README 'What is not in it': 'Single sign-on for a whole organization (SAML, or making a team sign in one way)'. src/server/oidc.ts signs individuals in with Google or Microsoft only; no SAML, no domain claim, no SCIM endpoint (grep).
added.docusign_tier: Account settings singleSignOnEnabled, allowOrganizationSsoManagement, allowOrganizationDomainUserManagement, requireExternalUserManagement (organisation administration); plan tier not confirmed
added.honesty_risk: Do not list an identity provider as supported until it has been tested end to end; a claimed domain must be proven by DNS before it changes anyone's login.
added.provider_notes: Open standards: SAML 2.0 (node-saml or samlify, MIT), OpenID Connect (oidc.ts already does the code flow), SCIM 2.0 for provisioning. Often a procurement requirement for public bodies. May overlap the Admin API entries of the platform area, which were cut off in the inventory I received.

added.name: Signers must log in to sign
added.what: An account can require that every signer logs in to an account before signing, or send only to recipients who have an account.
added.ours_evidence: Signers never need an account (README 'No account and no app needed'); a member of the same team who is a recipient also signs by link. No setting found (grep signer_must, must_login).
added.docusign_tier: Account settings signerMustLoginToSign, signerMustHaveAccount; plan tier not confirmed
added.honesty_risk: It proves the signer controlled that login at that time, as strong as the login itself (password, two-step, single sign-on); record which on the certificate. Useful for internal approvals in a public body, not a substitute for identity checks of outsiders.

added.name: Preview what a recipient will see
added.what: Before sending, the sender opens the signing page exactly as a chosen recipient will see it.
added.ours_evidence: The review step (src/components/editor/StepReview.tsx) lists problems and warnings but has no recipient preview (grep 'preview as' finds nothing); the editor shows all fields of everyone.
added.docusign_tier: API (/envelopes/{envelopeId}/views/recipient_preview, /templates/{templateId}/views/recipient_preview) and web app 'Preview and Send'
added.honesty_risk: A preview must never record a view, consent or signature in the audit trail or use a signature.

added.name: Delete and rotate pages of a document before sending
added.what: The sender removes a page or turns it the right way in the prepare screen or through the API, without uploading a new file.
added.ours_evidence: The editor offers 'Replace file' (src/components/editor/StepAdd.tsx:85) and phone photos are turned upright on upload (src/components/editor/photos.ts), but there is no page delete or rotate in the editor or the API (grep rotate/delete page finds nothing).
added.docusign_tier: API (DELETE .../documents/{documentId}/pages/{pageNumber}, PUT .../page_image rotate)
added.honesty_risk: Only before anyone has signed; the document hash shown on the certificate must be of the changed file and the history should say a page was removed.

added.name: Document reading zones for screen readers and OCR of scanned pages
added.what: Senders mark reading zones so screen readers read a document in the right order (Document Accessibility), and scanned documents can be OCRed so their text is searchable and readable.
added.ours_evidence: The signing page's Text view reads extracted text page by page (src/components/sign/TextView.tsx), and scanWarning in src/lib/scans.ts tells the sender that pages with no real text cannot be read to screen reader users, searched or used by 'Find fields for me'. No OCR (grep ocr/tesseract finds nothing), no reading-order zones, and no accessibility statement or conformance report page (grep WCAG, VPAT, EN 301 549 in src finds nothing).
added.docusign_tier: envelopeDefinition.accessibility (needs Document Accessibility enabled), accountSettingsInformation.allowOcrOfEnvelopeDocuments (no description in the spec); plan tier not confirmed
added.honesty_risk: OCR text can be wrong; it is a reading aid, the signed record is the page image. Do not claim WCAG, Section 508 or EN 301 549 conformance without an audit.
added.provider_notes: Tesseract or tesseract.js (Apache 2.0) or OCRmyPDF (MPL 2.0), self-hosted. Public buyers usually ask for an Accessibility Conformance Report (VPAT) as well; I could not fetch DocuSign's own report page to cite it.

added.name: PDF/A conversion of completed documents
added.what: Completed documents are converted to PDF/A for long-term archiving.
added.ours_evidence: renderEnvelopePdf in src/server/pdf.ts:615 builds the signed file with pdf-lib and saves it; no PDF/A metadata, OutputIntent or conformance check (grep 'pdf/a', 'pdfa' finds nothing).
added.docusign_tier: Account setting enablePDFAConversion (no description in the spec); plan tier not confirmed
added.honesty_risk: Do not call a file PDF/A until a validator such as veraPDF passes it. Conversion must happen before the fingerprint and certificate are made, or /verify will not match.
added.provider_notes: veraPDF (open source) to validate. pdf-lib can add XMP metadata and an OutputIntent, and fonts are already embedded; transparency in stamps and images may need flattening. Ghostscript can convert but is AGPL. National archives often require PDF/A for permanent records.

added.name: Require TLS for outgoing email
added.what: An account setting makes envelope emails go only over encrypted connections.
added.ours_evidence: src/server/mail.ts:41-53 hands every email to nodemailer through SMTP_URL; there is no requireTLS option and no setting. Whether the last hop to the recipient's server is encrypted is left to the relay.
added.docusign_tier: Account setting enforceTlsEmails (no description in the spec); plan tier not confirmed
added.honesty_risk: We can require TLS to our relay; say what the mail provider guarantees for delivery onward, and never say emails are end-to-end encrypted.
added.provider_notes: A relay that supports REQUIRETLS (RFC 8689) or per-message TLS enforcement; MTA-STS on the receiving side. The operator chooses and configures it.

added.name: External signature pads for in-person signing
added.what: The account uses hardware signature pads (Topaz, ePad, IntegriSign) for recipients who sign at a counter.
added.ours_evidence: The draw pad takes pen input through browser pointer events (pens.down(e.pointerId, e.pointerType, ...) in src/components/SignaturePad.tsx:170), so a pen tablet that acts as a pointer works; no vendor pad SDK, no pad setting.
added.docusign_tier: Account settings allowExternalSignaturePad, externalSignaturePadType (topaz, e_padv9, e_pad_integrisign, topaz_sigplusextlite); Admin only
added.honesty_risk: Pad strokes are not a biometric identity check unless someone analyses them; do not call it a biometric signature.
added.provider_notes: Vendor drivers or local web services on the counter computer (Topaz SigWeb, Wacom SDK). Useful at public service counters.

added.name: In-person ID check question recorded on the certificate
added.what: Before an in-person signing the host answers an admin-set question (for example which ID document they checked); the answer is saved and shown on the certificate.
added.ours_evidence: In-person signing locks the host's account in that browser (src/server/handover.ts, IN_PERSON_LOCK in src/lib/phone.ts:41) but asks the host nothing about the signer's identity (grep found no such question).
added.docusign_tier: Account setting inPersonIDCheckQuestion; Admin only
added.honesty_risk: Record it as the host's statement; we never see the ID. Do not store ID numbers unless the account needs them, and say how long they are kept.

added.name: Bring your own identity verification provider
added.what: An account plugs in its own identity verification service instead of DocuSign's partners.
added.ours_evidence: Only email and text one-time codes (CHECKS in src/lib/checks.ts:9). src/server/oidc.ts already implements an OpenID Connect code flow with PKCE and ID-token checks that could be pointed at an identity provider the account names.
added.docusign_tier: Account setting allowBYOIDV (no description in the spec); plan tier not confirmed
added.honesty_risk: Print only the claims that provider returned and its name; we cannot vouch for its assurance level.
added.provider_notes: Any OIDC identity provider the customer runs or contracts, for example a national login the public body already has.

added.name: Saved custom field library
added.what: Admins save custom fields (type, label, validation, size, font) once and reuse them across envelopes and templates.
added.ours_evidence: The editor palette is the fixed TYPES list in src/components/editor/shared.ts:7-16; fields can be duplicated within one envelope, not saved for reuse (no table in src/server/db.ts).
added.docusign_tier: API (/tab_definitions); plan tier not confirmed
added.honesty_risk: None special.

added.name: Access code generator and account rules for access codes
added.what: The app generates an access code for the sender, and admins set the format codes must follow.
added.ours_evidence: Codes are typed by the sender, at least ACCESS_CODE_MIN = 4 characters (src/lib/policy.ts:74), frozen after 10 tries. No generator and no account format rule. Codes are also stored as typed (src/server/db.ts:64) and compared raw (src/server/routes-sign.ts:207).
added.docusign_tier: Account settings enableAccessCodeGenerator, accessCodeFormat, allowAccessCodeFormat
added.honesty_risk: A code still only proves someone was told it.

added.name: Recipient provides their own phone number for a phone check
added.what: The sender can let the recipient type the phone number used for the phone or text check.
added.ours_evidence: The number for 'sms_code' is always the one the sender typed (src/lib/checks.ts, src/server/signercode.ts; README 'Checking who signs').
added.docusign_tier: Account settings phoneAuthRecipientMayProvidePhoneNumber, enableRecipientMayProvidePhoneNumber; Admin only
added.honesty_risk: A number the signer chose proves only that they hold some phone; the certificate must say who supplied the number.

added.name: Saved bulk send lists
added.what: A recipient list is saved once, reused for later sends and tested against a template before sending.
added.ours_evidence: POST /bulk/check is a dry run that reports problems and cost (src/server/routes-envelopes.ts), but each batch takes a pasted or uploaded CSV; no saved list (no table in src/server/db.ts).

batches.title: Word, OpenDocument and other office files become PDFs

batches.brief: Goal: a sender uploads the file they have and sees the PDF people will sign before placing fields. Read first: storeUpload, imageToPdf and extractPages in src/server/routes-envelopes.ts (the refusal 'Export Word or Google Docs files as PDF first'), src/components/editor/upload.ts and StepAdd.tsx, src/lib/scans.ts, the evidence pack in src/server/evidence.ts. 1. src/server/convert.ts recognises a file by its bytes, never its name: OOXML (a zip with [Content_Types].xml and word/, xl/ or ppt/), OpenDocument (a zip whose first entry is 'mimetype'), old Office files (D0 CF 11 E0), RTF (starts with an open brace, a backslash and rtf), HTML, plain text (valid UTF-8, no NUL), TIFF. Refuse a zip whose unpacked size passes 100 MB or 20 times its packed size. 2. Two converters, chosen by settings: CONVERTER=soffice runs LibreOffice headless here (a fresh profile folder per job with -env:UserInstallation, --convert-to pdf, CONVERT_TIMEOUT_MS default 60000 that kills the whole process group, at most CONVERT_MAX_JOBS at once in a queue, temporary files removed), or CONVERTER_URL points at a Gotenberg service (MIT) inside the operator's network. With neither, uploads behave as today and the refusal names the file types that need a converter. The converter must run without network access, because a document can point at remote pictures: README says how (a separate user with outbound traffic blocked, unshare -n, or Gotenberg in a container with no network). 3. storeUpload converts first, then goes on exactly as for a PDF (page limit, text for search, scan warning). The original is kept as a stored file linked to the document (encrypted like any file); the converted PDF is what is signed. Audit line: 'Converted from Contract.docx (SHA-256 ...) to PDF by LibreOffice <version>'. The evidence pack carries the original. 4. Words next to the converted pages: always 'Converted from Contract.docx. Check every page: the PDF is what people sign, and conversion can move text.'; tracked changes or comments in a Word file (w:ins, w:del, comments.xml): 'This file has tracked changes or comments. batches.title: A digital seal on every completed PDF
features: Tamper-evident PKI seal on completed documents
PAdES signature format (B-B and B-T)
Trusted timestamps (RFC 3161) on the seal
batches.brief: Goal: anyone can open a completed PDF in Acrobat or another reader and see that it has not changed since we completed it, without asking us. Read first: buildFinal and buildPdf in src/server/envelopes.ts (the one place the signed file is made and its SHA-256 stored), renderEnvelopePdf and drawCertificate in src/server/pdf.ts, POST /public/verify in src/server/routes-account.ts, src/app/verify, CHAIN_TRUTH and MATCH_MEANS in src/lib/evidence.ts, src/app/security/page.tsx. 1. src/server/finalpipe.ts: finishPdf(envelope, pdf) runs the steps that turn the rendered PDF into the stored one; today only the seal. buildFinal calls it (one line), so later steps (pdfa, eseal, qtsp, visibility) join here and the stored hash is always of the finished file. 2. src/server/seal.ts: an invisible approval signature (SubFilter ETSI.CAdES.detached, PAdES baseline B-B) over the whole file: add the signature field and dictionary with pdf-lib before saving, a fixed-size Contents placeholder and a ByteRange, save, hash the byte ranges with SHA-256, put the CMS SignedData into Contents. Build the CMS with a small DER writer of our own on node:crypto (src/server/der.ts) with the signed attributes PAdES needs (content-type, message-digest, signing-certificate-v2) and the signing time in the M entry; check each against ETSI EN 319 142-1 and name the clause in a comment. A reviewed library (@signpdf with node-forge) is acceptable instead if our own code does not validate within two days. 3. The key: SEAL_P12 and SEAL_P12_PASSWORD, or SEAL_KEY_PEM, SEAL_CERT_PEM and SEAL_CHAIN_PEM, behind a signer interface (sign(hash) returns the signature) so a cloud KMS or an HSM can be added later without the key on disk. RSA 2048 or more, or ECDSA P-256. 4. B-T: when TSA_URL is set, an RFC 3161 time-stamp token over the signature value goes in the unsigned attributes (src/server/tsa.ts; TSA_USER and TSA_PASSWORD optional). Without it the seal is B-B and the certificate says the time is our server's clock. 5. One line on the certificate, from a function in seal.ts that drawCertificate calls: 'This file carries a digital seal applied by <certificate name> when it was completed. A reader such as Acrobat can check that the file has not changed since. It does not show who stood behind each signature.' 6. /verify: when a dropped file carries our seal, also check it (digest, signature, the configured certificate) and say so; the byte-for-byte answer stays. /security and /security/certificate explain what the seal shows, and that Acrobat shows 'validity unknown' unless the certificate is on the Adobe Approved Trust List or the EU trusted list, which is the operator's purchase. 7. Envelopes completed before this are not sealed again: their fingerprint is in emails people hold. Honest words: a basic electronic seal of the server; never advanced, qualified, or a signature of the people who signed. Tests (tests/seal.test.ts): pdfsig (poppler, installed here; skip if missing) reports the signature valid and covering the whole file; openssl cms -verify on the extracted Contents; one changed byte makes it invalid; a stub TSA made in the test gives B-T and its token verifies; with no settings the output is byte for byte what it was; the stored SHA-256 is of the sealed file and /verify matches it. Settings: SEAL_P12, SEAL_P12_PASSWORD, SEAL_KEY_PEM, SEAL_CERT_PEM, SEAL_CHAIN_PEM, TSA_URL, TSA_USER, TSA_PASSWORD. Leave out: long-term validation and the audit chain time-stamp (seal-ltv), PDF/A (pdfa), organisation seals (eseal). House rules: read before editing, re-read before each edit (others edit too); in shared files (sign page, envelopes.ts, pdf.ts, settings page, db.ts, openapi.ts, README) small edits only, never reformat, logic in your own modules; tables and columns appended in db.ts; new route files imported in src/app/api/[...path]/route.ts and in openapi.ts; settings in .env.example; new words through t() once lang-core is in; plain words, no em dashes; check 390 and 320 px; npm test and npm run typecheck pass; README says exactly what was built.
batches.needs_from_operator: A document signing certificate and key (for the Acrobat green tick, one that chains to the Adobe Approved Trust List; for an EU qualified seal, a qualified certificate on a qualified device from a QTSP), and a time-stamp authority (FreeTSA for tests; a paid one for production).

batches.title: Archive copies of every email, and encrypted hand-over to the mail server
features: BCC email archive
Require TLS for outgoing email
batches.brief: Goal: a council's records officer or a freedom-of-information team gets a copy of every email the account sends about its documents, and nobody can sign from the archive. Read first: src/server/mail.ts (sendMail, recordMail, deliver, retries, renderMail), how the evidence pack takes links and codes out of stored emails (src/server/evidence.ts), src/server/bounces.ts. 1. Settings, Account, admins only (a component of yours in src/components/settings/, one line in the settings page): up to 5 archive addresses. Each is confirmed by a link sent to it before it receives anything, so nobody can archive into a stranger's inbox; one that bounces 3 times is shown to admins and paused. 2. Every email the account sends about an envelope (requests, reminders, deadline warnings, completed, declined, voided, corrected, comments, witness and group emails) also goes to each confirmed archive address as its own email, never as a Bcc header, with signing links, security codes and one-time codes replaced by '[link removed in the archive copy]', a first line 'Archive copy of an email sent to <address> on <time>', and the same attachments (the completed copy). 3. Archive emails are stored and retried like the others but never count to daily limits, never mark a recipient as bounced, and wait while sending is paused, like the rest. 4. Require TLS: SMTP_REQUIRE_TLS=1 makes nodemailer refuse to hand an email over to our relay without STARTTLS (requireTLS). README and /security say what this covers (the hop from our server to the mail provider) and what it does not (the provider's delivery onward, which MTA-STS and REQUIRETLS on the provider's side decide). 5. /security 'who can see what' lists archive addresses. API: GET, POST and DELETE /account/archive-addresses. Honest words: never say emails are encrypted end to end. Tests (tests/archivemail.test.ts): confirmation required, every kind of envelope email copied, no token, security code or one-time code anywhere in the copy (html and text), no copy for other accounts, limits not counted, pause respected, requireTLS passed to the transport (stub transport). Settings: SMTP_REQUIRE_TLS. Leave out: copies of billing and support emails. House rules: read before editing, re-read before each edit (others edit too); in shared files (sign page, envelopes.ts, pdf.ts, settings page, db.ts, openapi.ts, README) small edits only, never reformat, logic in your own modules; tables and columns appended in db.ts; new route files imported in src/app/api/[...path]/route.ts and in openapi.ts; settings in .env.example; new words through t() once lang-core is in; plain words, no em dashes; check 390 and 320 px; npm test and npm run typecheck pass; README says exactly what was built.

batches.title: A security record for admins, with alerts and export to a security system
features: Monitor: account activity tracking and alerts
Monitor API for SIEM export
batches.brief: Goal: an organisation's admin or security team sees who signed in and who changed what, and can feed it to their own security system. Read first: src/server/auth.ts, POST /auth/login and friends in src/server/routes-account.ts, src/server/routes-signin.ts, src/server/twostep.ts and two_step_log, member and API key routes in routes-account.ts and routes-trust.ts, src/server/webhooks.ts, the trigger that makes clickwrap_acceptances unchangeable (db.ts). 1. Table security_events: account id, time, who (user, API key, operator or the system), internet address, browser, kind, what it is about, details as JSON with no secrets (never a password, token, code or key). A trigger refuses UPDATE and DELETE except the purge after SECURITY_LOG_DAYS (default 400). 2. record(kind, ...) in src/server/seclog.ts, called with one line from each place: sign-in succeeded or failed (written to every account the person belongs to), signed out everywhere, password changed or reset, email changed, two-step on, off or reset, a Google or Microsoft login connected or removed, member invited, joined, removed, role changed or left, owner handed over, API key made or revoked, an API key first used from a new internet address, webhook made, changed or removed, everything exported, envelope deleted, restored or purged, template rules changed, settings changed (the setting's name, old and new value when not personal), account closing started or undone, sending paused or resumed by an operator. 3. Settings, Security (a component of yours, admins only): newest first, filter by kind, person and dates, CSV download. 4. GET /api/account/security-events?after=<cursor>&limit= (up to 1,000) for admins and admin-scope API keys, in time order with a cursor, so a security system can pull it; and an opt-in webhook event security.event. 5. Words: 'The qualified signature is made by <provider>, a qualified trust service provider. <product> carries it and shows the provider's check.' Account setting 'Let the AI read document text' (admins), off by default; the screen names the model, its host and the host's country; /security and /security/processing list it. With it off, nothing here sends anything. 2. Suggested fields: in the editor, 'Suggest fields' sends page text with positions (never page images) for pages where nothing was found; the model answers JSON (type, page, box, role); every item is checked (inside the page, a known type, no overlap) and shown as a suggestion to accept one by one or all; nothing is placed without the sender. 3. Summary for signers: the sender may switch it on per envelope; made once per document version; shown in a panel beside the document, closed at the start, with 'Made by an AI. It may be wrong. It is not the agreement and not legal advice. Read the document.'; never in place of the document, never changes what is signed; the audit trail says a summary was shown. 4. Drafted message: 'Draft a message' writes a subject and message from the document names and the people (document text only when the setting allows); it passes the fake-notice filter and the sender edits it before sending. 5. A daily limit per account and a plain sentence when the model is down. Tests (tests/aiassist.test.ts) with a stub model: setting off means no call, suggestions checked and bad ones dropped, the summary panel words and audit line, the drafted message through the filter, limits. Leave out: answering legal questions, changing documents. House rules: read before editing, re-read before each edit (others edit too); in shared files (sign page, envelopes.ts, pdf.ts, settings page, db.ts, openapi.ts, README) small edits only, never reformat, logic in your own modules; tables and columns appended in db.ts; new route files imported in src/app/api/[...path]/route.ts and in openapi.ts; settings in .env.example; new words through t() once lang-core is in; plain words, no em dashes; check 390 and 320 px; npm test and npm run typecheck pass; README says exactly what was built.
batches.needs_from_operator: A host for the open model (the same settings as the AI helper) and its cost per account.

batches.title: Find dates and duties in signed agreements, with reminders
features: Agreement repository with extracted key terms and renewal reminders
batches.brief: Needs ai-assist and custom-fields. 1. With the AI setting on, after completion the sender can ask 'Find the dates and amounts': the model reads the completed text and proposes parties, start date, end date, renewal date, notice date and amounts, each with its page and the words it came from. 2. Each value shows 'Found by AI on page 3. Check it.' and stays a proposal until the sender confirms or corrects it; confirmed values become custom fields of the envelope. 3. Reminders: the sender chooses to be emailed N days before a confirmed end or notice date; nothing for unconfirmed values. 4. The envelopes list filters by these dates ('ending in the next 90 days') and exports a calendar file. Tests (tests/airepo.test.ts): stub model proposals, confirm and correct, reminders only for confirmed values, filter and calendar file. Leave out: obligation workflows, an intake desk. batches.title: Combine templates, and find the right template for an upload
features: Several templates in one envelope (composite templates)
Automatic template matching
batches.brief: Needs templates-lib. 1. Combine: an envelope can start from two or more templates: documents one after another, roles with the same name become one person, fields carried over; each template's rules (who can use it, wording lock) still hold for its own parts. API: template_ids. 2. Matching: when a PDF is uploaded, compare its text per page with the documents of templates the person may use (the text is already read at upload; shingles of 5 words, Jaccard similarity); above the account's threshold (80, 90 or 95 percent) offer 'This looks like <template> (92 percent alike). Use its fields?' and show what differs (pages, changed words). Never applied without the sender's yes. Tests (tests/tplcombine.test.ts): roles merged, locks kept per part, matching above and below the threshold, differences listed, no match offered from templates the person may not use. Leave out: matching scans without text. batches.title: Fields everyone on the envelope can fill in
features: Collaborative fields
batches.brief: Needs fields-kinds. 1. A text, choice, dropdown or tick-box field can be marked 'Anyone on this envelope can fill it in' instead of belonging to one person, optionally with 'ask for initials when changed'. 2. Each change goes in the audit trail with who and the value before; the signing page shows who last changed it. 3. Once anyone has finished, a change to a shared field is refused unless the sender allows it, and then everyone who had finished is asked to sign again (the existing sign-again rule); a later change never silently alters what an earlier signer agreed to. 4. The completed PDF prints the final value; the certificate lists the changes. Tests (tests/collab.test.ts): two people change it, the audit lines, refusal after a finish, the sign-again path, initials on change. Leave out: shared signatures. batches.title: Notarisation: a partner for remote notarisation, and a notary in the room
features: Notary On-Demand (notaries supplied by a partner)
Remote online notarisation (by hand-off to a partner)
In-person electronic notarisation flow
batches.brief: Needs eseal. Goal: an organisation that needs a document notarised can do it without leaving the product, and nothing is called notarised unless a notary did it. 1. Partner hand-off, off until set (NOTARY_PROVIDER, NOTARY_API_KEY, NOTARY_WEBHOOK_SECRET; Proof or OneNotary, United States only): 'Get this notarised' on a prepared or completed envelope sends the document into the partner's session; status from the partner's webhook; the notarised PDF it returns is stored as a separate document, 'Notarised by <provider>, notary <name, commission, state>'. 2. A notary in the room: a role 'notary' for a member who states their commission (name, number, state or country, end date). The signers sign in person on the notary's device; then the notary fills in a journal entry (document, signers, the identity document they saw as their statement, fee) and applies their seal: their stamp picture and, if they uploaded a certificate, a PAdES signature (eseal's machinery for a person). Only the notary can export their journal (CSV); it is kept for the years the notary sets. 3. Words: '<product> does not commission notaries or check commissions. Whether an electronic notarisation is valid depends on the notary's state or country.' Tests (tests/notary.test.ts): partner stub (start, webhook, returned document), the in-room flow, journal, seal signature valid, export only for the notary. Leave out: our own video notarisation. House rules: read before editing, re-read before each edit (others edit too); in shared files (sign page, envelopes.ts, pdf.ts, settings page, db.ts, openapi.ts, README) small edits only, never reformat, logic in your own modules; tables and columns appended in db.ts; new route files imported in src/app/api/[...path]/route.ts and in openapi.ts; settings in .env.example; new words through t() once lang-core is in; plain words, no em dashes; check 390 and 320 px; npm test and npm run typecheck pass; README says exactly what was built.
